perks.name: Galestorm
perks.description:
Upon Hero kill, gain a 20% boost to movement speed, for 10 seconds. 

Must land killing blow to activate.
perks.explanation: This perk is decent, and an alternative to other perks due to its generic usefulness on many assassin heroes. Helps rotations from one finished fight to the next, although executing the opponent eats into the duration of the buff.

perks.name: Devourer
perks.description:
Executions heal an extra +10 HP. 

Healing occurs at the kill time of the execution.
perks.explanation:
This perk is especially good on heroes with strong dash heavies who can punish rolls (e.g Warden, Shaman, PK). 

Synergizes extremely well with Remedy and Head Hunter, providing Shaolin and Shaman a potent perk setup. 

Has extra value on heroes with executions that have quick kill times. Post-nerf it heals the same amout as Remedy, making it strictly worse than that perk.

perks.name: Early Reaper
perks.description:
Upon spawn or revive, your next attack deals 30% extra damage. 

Applies to chip damage from blocked attacks, landed attacks, and damage dealing feats - against heroes or soldiers.
perks.explanation:
This perk is awful, as is its logical equivalent, Crush Them, as they both have a small single use benefit that isn't even guaranteed to work.

The best use is to boost the damage of high damage ranged feats, which can be easier to hit off spawn when you arrive at a fight.

perks.name: Endurance
perks.description:
Gain a 3% stamina cost reduction per renown level. 

Maximum 12% stamina cost reduction at max renown.
perks.explanation:
This perk is decent, and is an acceptable alternative to Head Hunter due to its generic utility. Great for characters who use zones or high stamina moves in their 4v4 gameplay.

Note: Does not stack with the feat: tireless.

perks.name: Survival Instinct
perks.description: When in critical health ( <25 HP), gain a 25% stamina cost reduction.
perks.explanation: This perk is very underwhelming, and encourages you to attack when you are low on HP, a situation where you would rather be turtling up to obtain revenge.

perks.name: Crush Them
perks.description:
Upon Hero kill, your next attack deals 30% extra damage.

Applies to chip damage from blocked attacks, landed attacks, and damage dealing feats - against heroes or soldiers.
perks.explanation: This perk is awful, as is its logical equivalent, Early Reaper, as they both have a small single use benefit that isn't even guaranteed to work. The best use is to boost the damage of high damage ranged feats, immediately after a kill, like a worse version of Bloodlust.

perks.name: Head Hunter
perks.description: For each unique Hero executed, maximum health is increased by +4 HP to a maximum of +16 HP.
perks.explanation: This perk is decent, and is an acceptable alternative to Endurance. Synergizes extremely well with Remedy and Devourer to give you increased value out of execution healing.

perks.name: Aegis
perks.description:
All shields received are boosted by 20%. Applies to shields given by feats, perks, boosts, and revenge. 

Note that revenge shields can never exceed your max health.
perks.explanation:
This perk is very mediocre in general, but is more justifiable in Breach where shields are more prevalent. 

Because revenge shield can never exceed your maximum health, you won't even get the full 20% extra shield unless you have >144 health, making this perk near enough useless for many characters

perks.name: Shields Up
perks.description:
Upon revive, gain a +25 HP shield that lasts for 15 seconds. 

(Also triggered by the Auto Revive feat)
perks.explanation: Post nerf, this perk has essentially been dumpstered - as not only is the situation you can get the shield in far less frequent, it will likely run out before you actually get into combat again.

perks.name: Bastion
perks.description:
When in a zone, or carrying an offering/banner, gain 10% damage resistance. 

Zones include capture points in Dominion, and archer points, healing zones, and near the ram in Breach.
perks.explanation: Beneficial for stalling in Dominion. Extremely practical in Breach, where the Healing Zone, nearby ram, and archer lane are all considered objectives.

perks.name: Vengeful Barrier
perks.description: When exiting revenge, gain a +25 HP shield for 15 seconds.
perks.explanation:
This perk is easily the best defense perk, and rewards you even more for obtaining revenge. A must-have for any character with it available.

The addition of a timer for the shield duration is hardly a nerf, as you're normally still fighting when you exit revenge.

perks.name: Last Stand
perks.description: When in critical health ( <25 HP), gain 40% damage resistance.
perks.explanation:
This perk is quite good, with frequent debates about using it or Bulk Up, the perk combos incredibly well with Vengeful Barrier and shield feats, as they do not count towards the critical health threshold, giving you a massive amount of damage reduced health. This perk doesn't synergise too well with Bastion or Hard to Kill, considering that damage resistance does NOT stack.

The perk is only triggered once you are actually at critical health, so attacks that would kill from above critical health will not be reduced, (eg. a 30 damage heavy will still kill you from 30 hp) although this is less of a downside now that attacks do less damage overall.

The damage resistance provides an effective ~10HP boost once you are in critical, but the mental play of 40% damage resistance should not be ignored, as many players will neglect to try calculate their reduced damage, leading to them feeding revenge in an attempt to finish you off - allowing the script to be easily reversed.

perks.name: Fresh Focus
perks.description: When out of stamina, blocks, parries, and counter guard breaks recover 20% stamina.
perks.explanation:
This perk is decent, and a decent alternative to Endurance. It has been buffed to give stamina back on a CGB when OOS, as well as blocks and parries. 

Can now be very useful to relieve OOS pressure from bash/GB mix-ups, as well as from characters whose OOS pressure comes from fast follow-up attacks after a blocked light (eg. chain 400ms lights, light -> bash mix-ups etc)

perks.name: Bulk Up
perks.description:
Gain +4 HP maximum health per renown level. 

Maximum +16 HP at max renown level.
perks.explanation:
A consistent and reliable health increase, this perk is pretty good, with it's only downside being that you typically have to choose between this and Last Stand.

This perk doesn't synergise with the revenge shield bug, but does allow for more riskier plays/trades with the extra +16 HP.

perks.name: Radiant Rebound
perks.description: Upon spawn or revive, gain a 20% boost to movement speed for 10 seconds.
perks.explanation:
This perk is very good in Dominion on heroes who clear the minion/soldier lane, and allows you to get there at the start of a game faster than heroes who do not have the perk.

The ability to rotate quickly from spawn should not be underestimated, especially with the removal of defender renown. Stalling on an enemy's point is incredibly easy with this perk.

perks.name: Remedy
perks.description: Upon Hero kill, gain +10 HP. Must land the final hit to count.
perks.explanation: This perk is decent because of its generic use, and usually because alternatives are simply inferior. Synergizes extremely well with Head Hunter and Devourer to give you an increased value out of execution healing.

perks.name: Feline Agility
perks.description:
Gain +4% movement speed when reaching renown level 1, and +2% for each subsequent level. 

Maximum +10% movement speed at max renown level.
perks.explanation: This perk is very mediocre due to the low movespeed bonuses and being gated by renown level, which is especially a concern in Dominion. Not terrible, but outshined by many other feats typically.

perks.name: Supersonic
perks.description:
In revenge, gain +15% movement speed and uninterruptible sprint. 

This remains active for 10s after revenge ends.
perks.explanation: This perk is fairly mediocre despite giving you a free escape route in most scenarios. It is outshined by feats that more directly synergize with playstyles of heroes who can use it.

perks.name: Clever Tactics
perks.description:
Capture zones and use banners/offerings 15% faster. 

Zones affected are capture points in Dominion, and archer points and healing zones in Breach.
perks.explanation: This perk is pretty useless in Dominion, and can be useful for heroes who like to play the Archer lane in Breach. Typically outshined by other available perks.

perks.name: Rising Dawn
perks.description: Revive allies to 75% HP. (Instead of 50%)
perks.explanation:
This perk is good, especially on heroes with revive-related feats (e.g Speed Revive and Protected Revive). Valuable in Breach, as HP is a commodity.

Providing an extra 25% on all revives makes them somewhat worth-while in Dominion, meaning that you could try to get more renown from revives.

perks.name: Rapid Refresh
perks.description:
Upon hero takedown (kill or assist), or when reviving an ally, all feat cooldowns are reduced by 5%. 

Applies to active feats, and passive feats that have cooldowns.
perks.explanation: This perk is arguably the best in the game (besides Vengeful Barrier with the revenge shield bug), but is only available to a small amount of heroes. Greatly benefits these heroes if they use feats with cooldowns, rather than passives, allowing for more uses of their actual feats.

feats.name: Death Toll
feats.description: Passive | Killing Soldiers and Pikemen now grants you 3 Health and 3 Stamina
feats.explanation: A better body count - use it. Warden's other T1 options are far more conditional.

feats.name: Conqueror
feats.description: Passive | Capturing control zones is now 15% faster, and boosts last 20% longer.
feats.explanation:
Near enough useless in Dominion but can have a slight use in Breach on attackers, as capturing the Archers zones 15% faster is mildly useful - although with the faster capturing since the recent breach changes, the benefit is reduced. 

Additionally Breach has boosts which this feat improves the duration of.

feats.name: Come at Me
feats.description: For 30 seconds, you gain 50% more renown and gain 20hp on hero kill, but you take 20% more damage.
feats.explanation: Can be used in the minion lane greatly increasing your renown gain for killing soldiers. Allows you to reach your higher tier feats very quickly. In Breach, using this just before killing the Guardian will give you a huge amount of renown.

feats.name: Enfeeble
feats.description: Passive | Hitting an opponent with Shoulder Bash reduces their damage by 10% for 10 seconds
feats.explanation: Conceptually a good feat, but the damage negation isn't as valuable as running Inspire for a teamfight, or using Thrilling Comeback thanks to its large heal and bleed/fire cleansing.

feats.name: Inspire
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, you and your allies within a 10 meter AOE deal 20% more damage. 

This also causes the soldiers near you to fight faster and sprint forward.
feats.explanation:
A good damage buff, with a decent duration, that can give a significant advantage to your team in a team fight. The fairly quick cooldown allows you to use it without hesitation. 

In Breach, it gains another level of utility as the damage and attack speed boost also applies to pikemen. 

As a defender, this can be used to do huge damage to the ram, and for both teams it can make a crowd of allied pikemen far more lethal.

feats.name: Thrilling Comeback
feats.description: Passive | Upon unlocking, gives you a cleansing 20 health when you are in Revenge (so you gain the health if you unlock the feat while in revenge).
feats.explanation: A shadow of it's former self, it relies on you getting revenge to get any value, and is typically overshadowed by other feats due to its harsh nerf from 40 to 20 health. Use only if your other options suck.

feats.name: Total Recovery
feats.description: Passive | Whenever you revive an ally, they return at full Health instead of Half Health
feats.explanation: Reviving is rarely optimal, this feat allows you to brute force revives and give your teammate a chance, but they'll still be easier to track via rotations, and likely be stuck in a fight right after reviving, rather than helping your team's macro play. This also eats up a T3 slot, which could be used for better things, like Second Wind or Pugno Mortis. A fun feat idea, especially if it ever was paired with quick revive, but unlikely to see real use.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow. 

The feat can almost completely negate damage over time feats like Nail Bomb or Fire Flask, or punishes from bleed-based characters. 

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Pugno Mortis
feats.description: Throw a grenade, that explodes after 1600ms, dealing 40 damage to everyone in the 8 meter AOE.
feats.explanation:
Does a respectable chunk of damage over a large area, making it useful despite its nerfs. Easy to avoid on a lone opponent, unless they are OOS. 

In a team fight, can be effective to break up a group of opponents, or interrupt a revive, execution, or longer attacks (even works on Protected Revive and Hitokiri's executions). 

Be careful of friendly fire damage. Can be used to clear mid from some capture points if necessary. With the health nerf to Breach NPCS, this feat can now one-shot pikemen, allowing you to clear a whole wave very quickly, which can be rather useful.

feats.name: Trebuchet
feats.description: Call a quick Trebuchet strike to deal 70 damage over an area.
feats.explanation: A good feat for finishing off a single target, or adding in damage before jumping into a teamfight, but it competes against Morale Booster, which likely will see more value if your entire team is in a fight.

feats.name: Stalwart Banner
feats.description:
Place a banner which persists until the 20 second duration is over, creating an 8m AOE around it where all allies continuously regain health totaling 84 over 20 seconds. 

This also cleanses fire and bleed.
feats.explanation:
The health recovery from Stalwart Banner is not particularly fast, but it can still make a difference in a group fight, and can impact the match outcome if used whilst breaking. 

The heal tends to provoke aggression from your opponents, which can be exploited. Clearing bleed and fire damage can completely neuter some characters if they attack in range of the banner, and counters some feats like Sharpen Blade and Fire Flask. 

Depending on your team's T4 picks, it can be beneficial to pick this feat over another damage-dealing feat. 

In Breach, it is a very strong choice due to the scarcity of healing, and because it can also heal the Commander - although be sure to use it when there are no Pikemen around to distract his AI.

feats.name: Morale Booster
feats.description: Boosts the damage of you and all of your allies on the map by 30% for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A feat that gives a good damage boost to your entire team, regardless of where they are on the map. The 20s duration requires intelligent use, but it can be instrumental to finish off a breaking team without a chance for them to rally - especially because it boosts ally feat damage. 

As well as team fights, it can help an ally being ganked before you arrive to help. 

In Breach, it is fantastic for attackers when you get to the commander phase, as the cooldown is short enough to often allow it to be used a second time in the phase if necessary, and also boosts the damage of an ally on the ballista.

feats.name: Speed Revive
feats.description: Passive | Revives are 33% faster (ie. take 2.7 seconds instead of 4 seconds).
feats.explanation: A decent feat, can let you revive an ally more easily in a team fight, or with nearby enemy soldiers or pikemen.

feats.name: Conqueror
feats.description: Passive | Capturing control zones is now 15% faster, and boosts last 20% longer.
feats.explanation:
Near enough useless in Dominion but can have a slight use in Breach on attackers, as capturing the Archers zones 15% faster is mildly useful - although with the faster capturing since the recent breach changes, the benefit is reduced. 

Additionally Breach has boosts which this feat improves the duration of.

feats.name: Body Count
feats.description: Passive | Killing a soldier or pikeman through any means (including feats) grants you 1 health and 1 stamina.
feats.explanation:
A decent pick for mid lane characters in Dominion, this feat allows for some sustain whilst clearing minions, but is no longer really enough to stay in mid indefinitely. 

In Breach, this feat is extremely underwhelming, as you have to kill 10 pikemen to heal a single poke's worth of damage. 

May allow you to clear a bit more before having to head to the heal zone, but many other Tier 1s are superior in this mode.

feats.name: Juggernaut
feats.description:
For 10 Seconds, your movement speed is slowed and you cannot sprint. 20% damage reduction, auto counter guard break, uninterruptible.

Anomalously, Lawbringer and Warlord have 100ms and 800ms recoveries respectively, compared to the 600ms of others.
feats.explanation:
If an enemy is foolish enough to attack you whilst you have Juggernaut active, you can GB them in their attack recovery much like Shugoki's old passive superarmour, or punish them with an attack. 

With most characters nowadays having good gap-closers, rolling away from an opponent who has popped juggernaut is not always an option - unless you are facing Lawbringer or Conqueror. 

Due to the nerfed damage reduction, this feat no longer makes you nigh unkillable, so care must be taken to activate it whilst you have enough health to trade with. It still has good utility to stall in a zone, prevent a coordinated gank, or to disrupt in mid when the opponent is forced to engage or else lose the point.

It is far less useful in Breach, where stalling objectives is less important. However it does let you get a revive or execution uninterrupted by pikemen, which can be useful.

feats.name: Shield Basher
feats.description: Passive | Throws and shield based attacks now deal 6 Damage.
feats.explanation: Your neutral bashes will do 19 damage with this feat, and all your throws do 6 more damage too, making Conq's scary OOS pressure even more potent. By far the best choice.

feats.name: Fiat Lux
feats.description: Throw a flash grenade, which explodes after 1000ms, blinding anyone within the 6 meter AOE, dealing 5 damage, and removing all of their stamina.
feats.explanation:
Despite its quick cooldown, Fiat is rarely an optimal choice. It does a nominal amount of damage, so it can be used to clear minions from afar, but the AOE is not that impressive, and the slow throw animation means that it is easy to avoid, and difficult to captitalise on the stun. 

Unlike Kiai, if you are too close, you will stun yourself (or allies), so it is hard to use to escape a gank. Does have niche uses to prevent rolling away from a second AOE feat like Pugno Mortis, denying revives, or guaranteeing ally attacks, but has a high skill requirement for effective use.Feeds a /lot/ of revenge on hit, so be sure to use it on opponents that don't have revenge tags.

feats.name: Punch Through
feats.description: Passive | Doubles block damage. (From 18% to 36%)
feats.explanation: Blocked attacks do a bit more damage with this feat active, although still feed a lot of revenge. Chip damage cannot kill, so you still need to land a hit to finish off turtles. Overrides any other damage buffs that would otherwise affect chip damage.

feats.name: Heal on Block
feats.description: Passive | Blocking regenerates 4 Health.
feats.explanation:
The usefulness of this feat is fairly self-explanatory, and can discourage opponents from attacking you in a 1v1. 

Can also help survivabilty in ganks, as you can heal under the revenge shield. However, in practice, you still will take some chip damage from heavy attacks, and most competent opponents won't be throwing easily blockable lights anyway. 

No longer heals from minion or pikemen attacks, which removes its previous strength in mid.

feats.name: Uninterruptible
feats.description: You gain passive hyper armor for 30 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A nice duration with a decent cooldown, but the buff itself is pretty much pointless when being stalled. Its best use is in the midlane to allow for further unobstructed clear. Also allows for revives/executions in mid without minions interrupting. 

A big downside of passive hyperarmour is that it leaves conq vulnerable to much higher knockdown punishes than normal, as you will not experience early wake-up from any attack. 

In Breach, can have a niche use to allow you to carry or place the banner without being interrupted by pikemen or enemy attacks. 

However you will still be interrupted by bashes and GBs, so savvy opponents will still be able to stop you.

feats.name: Regenerate
feats.description:
Passive | Regenerate 15 health every 2 seconds. 

Must be out of guard, and not out of stamina, not sprinting, attacking or any other action, in order to start recovery. 

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.
feats.explanation:
An underwhelming feat that essentially requires you to not be playing the game in order to get any benefit from it - but does give a big benefit when it is active. 

The only things you can do whilst regenerating, are standing still, or walking. Even sprinting, or climbing a ladder, stops regeneration, so you cannot heal during rotations, unless walking rather than sprinting. 

Can have a niche use to regen health by unlocking at the edge of team fights, and is overall better now that the healing rate of capture zones has been reduced making it worth taking if you lack any better T4s. 

More useful in Breach, where you can walk forward with the ram, (or let it push you), or in Tribute when guarding an offering. But even then, a Tier 4 takes a long time to unlock, so you won't have much time to make use of it.

feats.name: Catapult
feats.description:
Call a catapult on the targeted 8 meter AOE, dealing 40-200 damage to everyone standing within it based on their distance to the center. 

Can only be used outside, and the projectile takes 2000ms to land and do damage.
feats.explanation:
A very underwhelming Tier 4 feat, as the time between the circle appearing and the catapult landing is enough to allow any opponent to escape the danger zone (unless they are unbalanced or blocked in by allies). 

Slightly more utility in Breach, as it can damage the ram, but does rather unimpressive damage to the commander, on the rare occasions he doesn't run out of the AOE.

feats.name: Crossbow Wound
feats.description: Fire a crossbow that deals 1+10 Bleed damage over 10s
feats.explanation:
The potential of this feat is to allow PK to function externally, but due to the speed of this feat and the Top Heavy soft feint to dagger cancel being UB, it's non essential, and you should likely take bounty hunter over it.

A short cooldown projectile feat - unlike the other ones that do 25 damage, it is twice as slow (being at 600ms over 300ms), but is still faster than most 40 damage projectile feats. 

A great choice to finish enemy players off, or to start off fights, as you the cooldown is low enough and the feat is a T1, allowing for a lot of uses, though you have to give up on bounty hunter for it. Makes getting your passive off a lot easier.

feats.name: Stealth
feats.description:
Passive | Hide yourself from the HUD, Radar & Aim Assist. 

Also hides you from the Oracle's Blessing in Tribute, Marked for Death and Scout
feats.explanation: Can help you to get a surprise attack in, and prevents many debuff feats from targetting you whatsoever. Assists against projectile feats by shortening the range of the snap-on crosshair.

feats.name: Bounty Hunter
feats.description: Passive | Gain 16 Health & full Stamina when you kill another Hero.
feats.explanation: Very useful in team fights or anti-ganking where landing a kill can heal you (even under a revenge shield) and allow you to carry on the offensive due to the full stamina regen, or save the need to rotate to a healing point. Even better in Breach, where healing is scarce.

feats.name: Bleed Armor
feats.description: After hitting a bleeding target, gain a 25% defense buff for 10 seconds
feats.explanation:
Allows PK to be strangely durable during fights, as the long effect of this feat means that enemies trying their best to gain the upper hand have a very uphill battle.

Consider Fiat Lux otherwise as PK's OOS pressure is insanely good.

feats.name: Executioner's Respite
feats.explanation:
Grants a minimal amount of extra healing from an execution, which is often useless if you are executing on an owned point, or have the Devourer perk active. 

You will only rarely get any value from this feat, so most characters have a stronger T2 available.

feats.name: Sanguine Serrations
feats.description:
For 12 seconds, all attacks deal an additional 10 bleed over 5 seconds.

Cooldown is reduced by 5 seconds for hitting a bleeding opponent while the feat is on cooldown.
feats.explanation:
An sidegrade to Sharpen Blade, one that provides half the uptime of the feat once activated to instead provide you with more uptime overall throughout the match by letting you reduce the cooldown of the feat.

Whilst a very strong effect, it does somewhat nerf the combo of Sharpen + Fear Itself (induced fear), as the latter feat is up for 20 seconds, instead of 12 (and 2 of those seconds are taken up by your recovery/running in time, really).

feats.name: Induced Fear
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, reduce the defense of all nearby enemies by 30% when active.

Duration of the feat resets on a kill.
feats.explanation:
A "sidegrade" to Fear Itself, where you trade 10% of the debuff's effect and a bit of range for the ability to reset the feat's timer on a kill - this feat is incredibly strong, and if your teammates let you last hit, you can have up to 80s of Fear Itself time (more even, if they're not breaking).

Potentially one of the best feats if you somehow get a kill in those 20s every time.

feats.name: Last Laugh
feats.description: Passive | Drop an explosive on death. Cannot activate if executed. Deals 20-100 damage depending on how far the enemy is from the center of the 10 meter AOE.
feats.explanation:
Because this feat requires your death, and can be prevented from working by an execution, it is somewhat underwhelming. 

Ensuring that you don't die prematurely or where the grenade is ineffective (eg. fall damage) can be challenging. But running into a gank, intentionally dying to a light attack, and getting a quad kill is possibly one of the most satisfying moments this game can offer. 

Because the commander's overhead unblockable will not execute, you can easily do great damage to him, and kill any defenders that are clustered nearby.

feats.name: Harsh Judgement
feats.description: For 30 seconds, opponent's attacks will cost 25% more stamina, stamina regen is slowed, OOS recovery is slowed.
feats.explanation:
Can be useful to help access LB's decent OOS pressure, and prevent opponents from clearing mid as quickly. Possibly more useful in Breach where LB's pikemen clear is lacking. 

Its best application is to give you an assist tag without applying a revenge stack, allowing you to build renown a bit faster.

feats.name: Body Count
feats.description: Passive | Killing a soldier or pikeman through any means (including feats) grants you 1 health and 1 stamina.
feats.explanation:
A decent pick for mid lane characters in Dominion, this feat allows for some sustain whilst clearing minions, but is no longer really enough to stay in mid indefinitely. 

In Breach, this feat is extremely underwhelming, as you have to kill 10 pikemen to heal a single poke's worth of damage. 

May allow you to clear a bit more before having to head to the heal zone, but many other Tier 1s are superior in this mode.

feats.name: Righteous Deflection
feats.description: Passive | 50% damage reduction after parrying, for 5 seconds.
feats.explanation: Halving incoming damage for 5 seconds after a parry can be rather useful when stalling in a gank situation, particularly against ganks that are set up from a parry, like Shaman's Bite.

feats.name: Fiat Lux
feats.description: Throw a flash grenade, which explodes after 1000ms, blinding anyone within the 6 meter AOE, dealing 5 damage, and removing all of their stamina.
feats.explanation:
Despite its quick cooldown, Fiat is rarely an optimal choice. It does a nominal amount of damage, so it can be used to clear minions from afar, but the AOE is not that impressive, and the slow throw animation means that it is easy to avoid, and difficult to captitalise on the stun. 

Unlike Kiai, if you are too close, you will stun yourself (or allies), so it is hard to use to escape a gank. Does have niche uses to prevent rolling away from a second AOE feat like Pugno Mortis, denying revives, or guaranteeing ally attacks, but has a high skill requirement for effective use.Feeds a /lot/ of revenge on hit, so be sure to use it on opponents that don't have revenge tags.

feats.name: Juggernaut
feats.description:
For 10 Seconds, your movement speed is slowed and you cannot sprint. 20% damage reduction, auto counter guard break, uninterruptible.

Anomalously, Lawbringer and Warlord have 100ms and 800ms recoveries respectively, compared to the 600ms of others.
feats.explanation:
If an enemy is foolish enough to attack you whilst you have Juggernaut active, you can GB them in their attack recovery much like Shugoki's old passive superarmour, or punish them with an attack. 

With most characters nowadays having good gap-closers, rolling away from an opponent who has popped juggernaut is not always an option - unless you are facing Lawbringer or Conqueror. 

Due to the nerfed damage reduction, this feat no longer makes you nigh unkillable, so care must be taken to activate it whilst you have enough health to trade with. It still has good utility to stall in a zone, prevent a coordinated gank, or to disrupt in mid when the opponent is forced to engage or else lose the point.

It is far less useful in Breach, where stalling objectives is less important. However it does let you get a revive or execution uninterrupted by pikemen, which can be useful.

feats.name: Protected Revive
feats.description: Passive | Grants a 75 health overshield to revived allies, which lasts for 15 seconds.
feats.explanation: Removal of hyperarmour from this feat means it no longer allows easier revives in mid or in team fights. Not only does this feat rely on you getting revives, your ally also has to be in combat within 15s of being revived to receive any benefit, making this feat so situational that it is basically useless.

feats.name: Pugno Mortis
feats.description: Throw a grenade, that explodes after 1600ms, dealing 40 damage to everyone in the 8 meter AOE.
feats.explanation:
Does a respectable chunk of damage over a large area, making it useful despite its nerfs. Easy to avoid on a lone opponent, unless they are OOS. 

In a team fight, can be effective to break up a group of opponents, or interrupt a revive, execution, or longer attacks (even works on Protected Revive and Hitokiri's executions). 

Be careful of friendly fire damage. Can be used to clear mid from some capture points if necessary. With the health nerf to Breach NPCS, this feat can now one-shot pikemen, allowing you to clear a whole wave very quickly, which can be rather useful.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow. 

The feat can almost completely negate damage over time feats like Nail Bomb or Fire Flask, or punishes from bleed-based characters. 

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Igneus Imber
feats.description:
Four charges of grenades, that explode 1600ms after landing, dealing 20-65 damage depending on how far the enemy is from the center of the 8 meter AOE. 

10 Second cooldown between first 4 uses. 180 second cooldown thereafter.
feats.explanation: Not as lethal as it's pre-nerf state, but still an imminently usable Tier 4, with multiple grenades doing rather decent damage in a good area.

feats.name: Catapult
feats.description:
Call a catapult on the targeted 8 meter AOE, dealing 40-200 damage to everyone standing within it based on their distance to the center. 

Can only be used outside, and the projectile takes 2000ms to land and do damage.
feats.explanation:
A very underwhelming Tier 4 feat, as the time between the circle appearing and the catapult landing is enough to allow any opponent to escape the danger zone (unless they are unbalanced or blocked in by allies). 

Slightly more utility in Breach, as it can damage the ram, but does rather unimpressive damage to the commander, on the rare occasions he doesn't run out of the AOE.

feats.name: Regenerate
feats.description:
Passive | Regenerate 15 health every 2 seconds. 

Must be out of guard, and not out of stamina, not sprinting, attacking or any other action, in order to start recovery. 

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.
feats.explanation:
An underwhelming feat that essentially requires you to not be playing the game in order to get any benefit from it - but does give a big benefit when it is active. 

The only things you can do whilst regenerating, are standing still, or walking. Even sprinting, or climbing a ladder, stops regeneration, so you cannot heal during rotations, unless walking rather than sprinting. 

Can have a niche use to regen health by unlocking at the edge of team fights, and is overall better now that the healing rate of capture zones has been reduced making it worth taking if you lack any better T4s. 

More useful in Breach, where you can walk forward with the ram, (or let it push you), or in Tribute when guarding an offering. But even then, a Tier 4 takes a long time to unlock, so you won't have much time to make use of it.

feats.name: Amplified Roar
feats.description: Lion's Roar Finisher now unbalances enemies.
feats.explanation:
Take Bounty Hunter or Body Count over this feat, any day of the week.

The concept of unbalancing enemies is a neat one, but tying it to such a stamina intensive, easily peelable and lengthy manuever is not one that you should waste your T1 on, I'd even use the GB to get a wallsplat into a pin and try to just use my punch if I /really/ wanted the eagles talons, and considering the strength of the T2, it's not particularly worth it.

feats.name: Bounty Hunter
feats.description: Passive | Gain 16 Health & full Stamina when you kill another Hero.
feats.explanation: Very useful in team fights or anti-ganking where landing a kill can heal you (even under a revenge shield) and allow you to carry on the offensive due to the full stamina regen, or save the need to rotate to a healing point. Even better in Breach, where healing is scarce.

feats.name: Eagle's Windfall
feats.description: After landing an Eagle's Talon, reduce (nearby?) enemies attack by 20% for 10 seconds, and buff nearby allies movement speed for 10 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A weird feat, it provides the inverse effect of Inspire to nearby enemies, and buffs your allies movement speed(???) - a very questionable buff for your team, and I'd much prefer to see ANY other status buff - as movement speed doesn't really do much in a fight.

Take Inspire over this.

feats.name: Inspire
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, you and your allies within a 10 meter AOE deal 20% more damage. 

This also causes the soldiers near you to fight faster and sprint forward.
feats.explanation:
A good damage buff, with a decent duration, that can give a significant advantage to your team in a team fight. The fairly quick cooldown allows you to use it without hesitation. 

In Breach, it gains another level of utility as the damage and attack speed boost also applies to pikemen. 

As a defender, this can be used to do huge damage to the ram, and for both teams it can make a crowd of allied pikemen far more lethal.

feats.name: Executioner's Respite
feats.explanation:
Grants a minimal amount of extra healing from an execution, which is often useless if you are executing on an owned point, or have the Devourer perk active. 

You will only rarely get any value from this feat, so most characters have a stronger T2 available.

feats.name: Vainglorious Pugio
feats.description:
A projectile that deals 15 damage and traps the enemy for 2 seconds.

Kicking the bound target unbalances them.
feats.explanation:
Fast activation and immobilises an opponent for long enough for you to land a kick into a light into a heavy for extra damage, or to even knock someone down for an eagles talons making it one of the best ranged feats that is usable in a 1v1.

The true strength of the feat however, is in a ganking situation, where it can enable one of Centurion's deadly coordinated ganks with an ally. Additionally, an opponent cannot pop revenge whilst pinned, allowing it to confirm a kill on an opponent with a high revenge build up.

Can also be used with a Raider, Warlord, or LB teammate to guarantee a ledge kill.

feats.name: Sharpen Blade

For 20 seconds, inflict 10 bleed damage (in 2 ticks of 5) on each hit.

Always has 1500ms total use duration (start-up + recovery time), but start up varies per-character. 

Shinobi/Peacekeeper have a 300ms startup. 
Centurion/Orochi/Valkyrie have a 500ms startup. 
Berserker/Aramusha have a 600ms startup.
Nobushi has a 700ms startup.
feats.explanation:
Significantly diminished from its pre-nerf state, if you can look past the very long cooldown, this feat can still give a nice boost to your damage. 

Multi-hit, or fast chain attacks only apply the bleed damage twice in a short interval. Suffers from being negated by Second Wind. Still powerful with a Shaman teammate.

feats.name: Refined Phalanx
feats.description: Grant a 70 health overshield to all alive teammates (yourself included) for 10 seconds, cleanse all negative status effects.
feats.explanation: One of the best feats in the game buffed to cleanse all debuffs, allowing you to completely negate T4s that provide harmful status effects, especially those like Juren's T4 - that end up actually debuffing the enemy team instead.

feats.name: Stalwart Banner
feats.description:
Place a banner which persists until the 20 second duration is over, creating an 8m AOE around it where all allies continuously regain health totaling 84 over 20 seconds. 

This also cleanses fire and bleed.
feats.explanation:
The health recovery from Stalwart Banner is not particularly fast, but it can still make a difference in a group fight, and can impact the match outcome if used whilst breaking. 

The heal tends to provoke aggression from your opponents, which can be exploited. Clearing bleed and fire damage can completely neuter some characters if they attack in range of the banner, and counters some feats like Sharpen Blade and Fire Flask. 

Depending on your team's T4 picks, it can be beneficial to pick this feat over another damage-dealing feat.

feats.explanation: The damage boost is only triggered on landed attacks, and isn't triggered by chip damage or by landing a bash, or guard break - however, with the improved openers on characters that have been reworked, and the CCU making attacks land more consistently across the board, this feat can give a fairly reliable damage buff, especially on high damage chain attacks.

feats.name: Boleadoras
feats.description: Projectile that deals 20 damage and traps an enemy for 2 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A slow and obvious start-up animation makes this feat underwhelming, and hard to land, although it can guarantee more damage than other projectiles if used correctly. 

At correct range, you can whiff or backstep a light into Skewer, which can guarantee a lot of extra damage, or even environmental kills. 

Can also guarantee a ledge kill with a coordinated ally Raider or Warlord, or a ganking move like Long Arm or Shaman Bite.

feats.name: Fear Itself
feats.description: Enemies around you take 40% more damage. 8 meter AOE that moves around with you and lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation: A good Tier 4 feat that can give your team a big advantage in a team fight, and can help anti-gank as well. Has great synergy with any feat that buffs damage.

feats.explanation: A shorter duration than Fear Itself, giving a smaller effective damage buff, which only affects your attacks, and not your teammates' attacks. The choice is obvious.

feats.name: Sinister Shield
feats.description: Grant an ally a 30 health shield that lasts for 8 seconds, at the cost of 30 damage to yourself.
feats.explanation:
Has a very long activation range and does not always need line of sight, so can be used from a zone to shield an ally at a distance, and quickly regain health. 

This means it is better on smaller maps. BP's T2 Healing Ward can regain the sacrificed health if you hang back in a team fight momentarily, and allows it to still be useful in Breach despite the scarcity of healing in general.

feats.name: Speed Revive
feats.description: Passive | Revives are 33% faster (ie. take 2.7 seconds instead of 4 seconds).
feats.explanation: A decent feat, can let you revive an ally more easily in a team fight, or with nearby enemy soldiers or pikemen.

feats.name: Healing Ward
feats.description: Passive | Regenerate 3 health per second whilst in Bulwark Stance.
feats.explanation:
Still one of the most powerful healing feat in the game, this is essentially a weaker version of Regenerate that can be used in combat, and is a Tier 2 instead of Tier 4. 

In team fights, allows you to easily back off and heal at a moment's notice, especially considering BP's decent walk speed and general safety whilst in Bulwark Stance. 

In Breach, this feat completely invalidates the need to go to the healing zone, as you can easily sit in a group of your pikemen, and heal to full in seconds.

feats.name: Doom Banner
feats.description:
Place a stationary banner that creates an 8 meter AOE thats debuffs enemy defense by 25%, and persists after your death. 30 second duration.

Anomalously, Berserker has 966ms activation time, and 1033ms recovery time compared to the listed values of others.
feats.explanation:
The defence debuff that Doom Banner causes is very significant and enough to influence the outcome of a team fight. 

Clever placement near a choke point can ensure that the enemy team are all affected. 

The banner persists and can help your team after you die, and combined with the decent cooldown, means you do not have to worry about wasting its use if you are at low health.

feats.description: Removes an opponent's shield.
feats.explanation:

Has a secondary use in Breach, where the longer match allows more uses, and it can potentially stop an opponent from using a shield buff, or prevent the use of a shield on the commander.

feats.name: Tough as Nails
feats.description:
Passive | Raises max Health by 15% but does not heal when first unlocked. 

Subsequent respawns will give you full health (Except in Elimination).
feats.explanation:
More health is always nice. Combined with the Bulk Up and Bastion perks, can make you quite tanky and hard to dislodge from a capture point. It doesn't effect the amount of revenge build up you need to activate revenge, making stalling easier in comparison. 

Don't use it in Elimination, where for some reason, it doesn't work on respawn.

feats.name: Punch Through
feats.description: Passive | Doubles block damage. (From 18% to 36%)
feats.explanation: Blocked attacks do a bit more damage with this feat active, although still feed a lot of revenge. Chip damage cannot kill, so you still need to land a hit to finish off turtles. Overrides any other damage buffs that would otherwise affect chip damage.

feats.name: Umbral Shelter
feats.description:
Applies a 20 health shield that stacks to all allies within a 16 meter AOE, in 3 pulses. 

The shield lasts forever.
feats.explanation:
Gives your allies up to 60 shield for being next to you - helpful for saving them from damage, but is no longer the feat that provides functional immortality.

Applies in pulses, so using it mid teamfight might lead to some damage you take.

feats.name: Morale Booster
feats.description: Boosts the damage of you and all of your allies on the map by 30% for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A feat that gives a good damage boost to your entire team, regardless of where they are on the map. The 20s duration requires intelligent use, but it can be instrumental to finish off a breaking team without a chance for them to rally - especially because it boosts ally feat damage. 

As well as team fights, it can help an ally being ganked before you arrive to help. 

In Breach, it is fantastic for attackers when you get to the commander phase, as the cooldown is short enough to often allow it to be used a second time in the phase if necessary, and also boosts the damage of an ally on the ballista.

feats.name: Corruption Blade
feats.description:
Apply a coating to your weapon that lasts for 8s, and corrupts the first opponent that you hit for 10s. 

Corruption deals 8 damage per second to the opponent, and any of their allies (excluding soldiers) within a 10 meter AOE, as long as one of their allies is within range.
feats.explanation:
This feat has essentially the same effect as Nuxia's T4 feat, except available as a T1, and with just three quaters of the cooldown. 

Despite two nerfs this feat is still obscenely powerful for how quickly it is available. 

Synergy with Warmonger's T2 and T3 feats make this even more powerful as a match progresses. 

Even more powerful in Breach, as it can also be applied to officers and the commander. I don't know what the devs were smoking when they decided it was OK to give a T4 as a character's T1.

feats.name: Rush
feats.description: For 10 seconds, your sprint speed is boosted by 30%.
feats.explanation: A consistently useful feat. Can help with rotations or to get back into the fight after a respawn, especially on bigger maps, but there is often a better choice, especially on characters that are already fast. Can be useful to capture an offering in Breach or Tribute.

feats.name: Conqueror
feats.description: Passive | Capturing control zones is now 15% faster, and boosts last 20% longer.
feats.explanation:
Near enough useless in Dominion but can have a slight use in Breach on attackers, as capturing the Archers zones 15% faster is mildly useful - although with the faster capturing since the recent breach changes, the benefit is reduced. 

Additionally Breach has boosts which this feat improves the duration of.

feats.name: Elixir of Corruption
feats.description:
Passive | Heal 50% damage dealt to corrupted opponents. 

Includes damage dealt to the target of corrpution feats, but not damage dealt to opponents that enter the corruption AOE without also being corrupted themselves.
feats.explanation:
This feat can heal you a very large amount when damaging opponents corrupted by your T1 or T4 - including damage from the feat itself. The heal is so large that you will often regain full health when using your T4 feat. 

Due to very fast cooldown on your T1, you can make use of this feat in most encounters in a match. Also works on opponents corrupted by ally Warmongers (or Nuxias), making it exponentially more powerful the more warmongers are on your team - but who needs single pick, right?

feats.name: Arrow Strike
feats.description: Call a 45 damage arrow strike within a 6 meter AOE. Only works outside.
feats.explanation:
Slow speed can make it hard to hit with unless an ally confirms it, but it does good damage and has a fast cooldown. 

More useful in Breach where it can quickly kill a crowd of pikemen. Can no longer be i-framed, so is now consistent with all other AOE feats.

feats.name: Flesh Wound
feats.description:
Passive | After taking a hit receive 20% less damage for 3 seconds. Triggered by attacks or bashes hitting, being hit by a GB (even if countered), and any feat that causes hitstun. 

Not triggered by chip damage.
feats.explanation: Flesh Wound is strictly a worse version of Thick Skin, having all the same properties except granting 5% less damage reduction, but seeing as they both trigger much more consistently now, this feat is now quite a good feat, even though a better version exists.

feats.name: Power of Corruption
feats.description: Passive | All your attacks and feats deal 30% more damage against a target that is corrupted.
feats.explanation: A huge damage buff (same as Morale Booster) but available against any corrupted target, not only does this feat boost the damage of your corruption feats themselves, it also works on opponents corrupted by your allies, becoming exponentially more powerful the more Warmongers (or Nuxias) there are on your team.

feats.name: Corruption Blast
feats.description:
Causes any enemy in a 10m AOE centered on the Warmonger to get corrupted. 

Corruption deals 8 damage per second to the opponent, and any of their allies (excluding soldiers) within a 10 meter AOE, as long as there is an ally within range.
feats.explanation:
A powerful Tier 4 feat, this feat is essentially an "automatic anti-gank button", which becomes more powerful the more opponents are nearby. 

Has a maximum damage output more than 4 times as powerful than Nuxia's Infection feat, making her T4 look pretty pathetic in comparison. Being ganked by 4 players in a confined zone is essentially a guaranteed team-wipe - especially if used from a revenge parry which keeps multiple opponents on the ground. 

Has a very fast activation which causes hitstun and guarantees a zone or light attack. Excellent synergy with her T2 and T3 means you will often heal to full at the same time as killing all your opponents. 

Extremely powerful when attacking in Breach mode as it can apply to the Commander, and any defenders nearby, allowing you free reign to wail on him.

feats.name: Arrow Storm
feats.description:
5 waves of 50 damage arrow showers over a 15 meter AOE. 

First wave takes 1100ms to land, with each subsequent wave taking another 1300ms. 

Can only be used outside.
feats.explanation:
It can be hard to hit aware opponents with this feat, as it can be fairly easily avoided, unless they are engaged by allies. 

The large AOE makes it great for clearing mid, and it can kill a lot of pikemen, and do very good damage to the ram. One wave of arrows is rarely enough to kill an opponent, and the feat also does considerable friendly fire damage. 

However, with careful targeting it is still capable of wiping an entire team if they are badly positioned.

feats.name: Auto Revive
feats.description:
Passive | 2 seconds after dying, automatically revive at 50% HP. 

Cannot activate if executed or being killed by the evironment.
feats.explanation:
For Honor: Vikings Die Twice. 

Getting a second chance to not die is often useful, giving you even more stalling ability on a zone, letting you get back up and clinch a close duel that the opponent thought they'd won, or start reviving teammates killed by a ranged AOE damage feat. 

The element of surprise that this feat gives you can help you get a hit in on a careless or distracted opponent. 

Unfortunately, a match will end before you revive via this feat, although it does let you emote spam with your victorious opponents.

feats.name: Stern Stare
feats.description: Target an opponent to reduce their attack damage by 25% for 15 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Short cooldown means it is available regularly and can give you an edge in many different scenarios. If used on an opponent with revenge, it will mostly negate their damage boost, and if you are being ganked yourself, can be useful to apply to the opponent who is aiming to get in damage that the other opponent wants to set up for. 

Damage reduced attacks still feed the same amount of revenge as normal, so can increase surviveability in outnumbered situations, and it can negate or minimise the effect of other powerful feats, such as Fury or AOE damage feats.

feats.name: Speed Revive
feats.description: Passive | Revives are 33% faster (ie. take 2.7 seconds instead of 4 seconds).
feats.explanation: A decent feat, can let you revive an ally more easily in a team fight, or with nearby enemy soldiers or pikemen.

feats.name: Fast Recovery
feats.description: Passive | Stamina regenerates twice as fast. Also works when exhausted.
feats.explanation: Allows you to be a bit more aggressive with stamina-intensive attacks, and escape OOS state much faster. Also useful for zoning more frequently in mid lane or team fights. If you take this feat, there is no need to bother with the Fresh Focus perk.

feats.name: Draconite Mist
feats.description:
Heals self and all allies within 16 meter AOE for 15 health. 

Also cleanses bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Large AOE, low cooldown, nice heal amount for a T2, extremely quick activation, and also cleanses bleed or flame - this feat is very strong. 

It allows Gryphon's team to have a huge advantage in group fights, especially if the opponents include any bleed characters, and it can mostly negate several powerful AOE feats, like fire flask. 

Even more powerful in Breach due to scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Flesh Wound
feats.description:
Passive | After taking a hit receive 20% less damage for 3 seconds. Triggered by attacks or bashes hitting, being hit by a GB (even if countered), and any feat that causes hitstun. 

Not triggered by chip damage.
feats.explanation: Flesh Wound is strictly a worse version of Thick Skin, having all the same properties except granting 5% less damage reduction, but seeing as they both trigger much more consistently now, this feat is now quite a good feat, even though a better version exists.

feats.name: Winner's Advantage
feats.description: Passive | After a successful attack, you deal 20% more damage for 1.5 seconds.
feats.explanation:
In practice, this feat can give your follow-up attacks a decent boost if you can land a second attack in the short window. 

With the CCU improving the ability to land opener attacks, this feat is much more relevant. 

In Breach it gains some utility by letting chain heavies do more damage against pikemen.

feats.name: Draconite Bolt
feats.description:
Shoot a crossbow bolt at an enemy that does 20 damage, and if it hits, heals self and all allies within 16 meter AOE by 15 health. 

Also cleanses bleed and fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Still has a fast activation, but is now too slow to be guaranteed on a heavy parry - this projectile feat has a 35 health swing if it only heals the user, but is most powerful in group fights. 

Allows healing allies from a long range, if you can't make it to the fight in time, or long range peel within group fights. 

Combined with his T2, this means a single Gryphon will have a healing feat available in almost every team fight, but with multiple Gryphons around, it makes their team very hard to kill when grouped together.

feats.name: Tough as Nails
feats.description:
Passive | Raises max Health by 15% but does not heal when first unlocked. 

Subsequent respawns will give you full health (Except in Elimination).
feats.explanation:
More health is always nice. Combined with the Bulk Up and Bastion perks, can make you quite tanky and hard to dislodge from a capture point. It doesn't effect the amount of revenge build up you need to activate revenge, making stalling easier in comparison. 

Don't use it in Elimination, where for some reason, it doesn't work on respawn.

feats.name: Fury
feats.description: For 20 seconds, Raise sprint speed by 15%, attack by 20% and gain 20% damage reduction.
feats.explanation:
Gives a decent attack and defense boost, which can make a significant difference in a team fight, give you an edge in a 1v1, or let you anti-gank more effectively. 

The speed boost lets you pop the feat at a slight distance and quickly get in range to engage the enemy. The damage boost also affects feat damage, and synergises excellently with Fire Flask. Whilst this combo is no longer as effective after the nerfs both of these feats have received, it is still a very powerful tool.

feats.name: Draconite Cleanser
feats.description:
Throw a grenade that explodes after 900ms dealing 25-50 damage to all opponents within the X meter AOE, depending on distance from the center. 

1 second after the explosion, it spawns a healing zone of the same AOE, which heals 5 health per second to all allies within the zone. 

Heal zone lasts for 10 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Gryphon's T4 feat is surprisingly not entirely busted, as one might expect. The grenade does a reasonable amount of damage but is quite easy to avoid, and the AOE heal is good, but can only heal 50 health total, which is less than other healing T4s like Stalwart Banner. 

Be wary of using it at your own feet or thrown at an ally, because it does do friendly fire damage and can do significant damage to yourself, which undo any benefit of the heal. 

Like most healing feats, it is more powerful in Breach, and is particularly useful used within crowds of enemy pikemen.

feats.name: Champion's Aura
feats.description:
Cleansing heal that heals yourself and allies 100 health over 30 seconds in a 12 meter AOE centered on you, that follows you around. 

This feat's activation is uninterruptible.
feats.explanation:
Similar to Stalwart Banner, with a larger heal over a longer period, but it will not persist if you die. However, the fact that the heal AOE follows you gives it a bit more flexibility, and potential use if you and a teammate are retreating from a fight. 

More useful in Breach, particularly because you can follow the Commander around if he decides to leave the healing zone to kill pikemen, like the big psycho that he is.

feats.name: Rush
feats.description: For 10 seconds, your sprint speed is boosted by 30%.
feats.explanation: A consistently useful feat. Can help with rotations or to get back into the fight after a respawn, especially on bigger maps, but there is often a better choice, especially on characters that are already fast. Can be useful to capture an offering in Breach or Tribute.

feats.name: Tireless
feats.description: Passive | Actions use 17% less stamina.
feats.explanation:
Allows you to attack a bit more frequently, but not all that impressive.

Note: Does not stack with the perk: endurance.

feats.name: Body Count
feats.description: Passive | Killing a soldier or pikeman through any means (including feats) grants you 1 health and 1 stamina.
feats.explanation:
A decent pick for mid lane characters in Dominion, this feat allows for some sustain whilst clearing minions, but is no longer really enough to stay in mid indefinitely. 

In Breach, this feat is extremely underwhelming, as you have to kill 10 pikemen to heal a single poke's worth of damage. 

May allow you to clear a bit more before having to head to the heal zone, but many other Tier 1s are superior in this mode.

feats.name: Marked For Death
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, target's position is revealed on the map for all allies and their defense is lowered by 15% and attacks take 25% more stamina. 

You also receive 50% more renown on their death (assists count as well).

Can be negated by Stealth.
feats.explanation:
A decent debuff that can swing a 1v1 or help get rid of a troublesome opponent in a team fight. Long cooldown and fairly short duration is the biggest drawback. 

This feat is completely negated by stealth, so do NOT use it on a hero with stealth.

feats.name: Inspire
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, you and your allies within a 10 meter AOE deal 20% more damage. 

This also causes the soldiers near you to fight faster and sprint forward.
feats.explanation:
A good damage buff, with a decent duration, that can give a significant advantage to your team in a team fight. The fairly quick cooldown allows you to use it without hesitation. 

In Breach, it gains another level of utility as the damage and attack speed boost also applies to pikemen. 

As a defender, this can be used to do huge damage to the ram, and for both teams it can make a crowd of allied pikemen far more lethal.

feats.name: Bear Trap
feats.description:
Set a trap with a 4 meter AOE, that deals 25 damage, pins the target in place for 2 seconds and leaves them unable to block, parry or dodge. Can only have one Bear Trap active at a time.

1400ms activation time for Berserker/Shaman, 2700ms activation time for Raider.
feats.explanation:
A great feat for defending a zone, or protecting yourself as you clear mid, as in addittion to the damage, it can guarantee a heavy attack or ledging bash. 

Maintains the Out of Lock state, which can guarantee a large punish if the opponent was unlocked before they were caught. 

Can even be used in combat with a little finesse. Like all traps, the damage log can be used to tell you that it has been triggered at a distance. 

The main disadvantages are the long cooldown, and that it is fairly easy to avoid if spotted, so make sure to hide it in scenery as best you can.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow.

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.description:
On activation, causes all enemy soldiers within a 21 meter AOE to flee. 

All allies across the map gain a 25% attack damage boost that lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Can give your entire team a good damage boost to turn a team fight in your favour. The soldier fleeing effect super useful too, as it essentially gives you a free cap on the mid lane, and enables easier executions and revives there. 

In Breach it is useful for the damage boost in a team fight or when attacking the Commander, but for some reason the fleeing effect does not work on Pikemen or Archers, reducing its utility.

feats.name: Fire Flask
feats.description: Throw a projectile that explodes in fire after 1100ms, dealing 20-30 damage within the 10 meter AOE and then 10 fire damage per second over 10 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Despite nerfs, this feat is still a great Tier 4, as it is hard to avoid, can be used inside, and has a big area denial affect. The direct damage is now less likely to kill opponents instantly, but the damage over time and area denial aspects have not been changed, allowing great control of a fight.

Combine with a damage buffing feat (eg. Fury or Inspire) or a defence debuff feat to maximise its potential. If used where opponents cannot get out of the flames, it can still wipe an entire team, but the fire damage can be cleansed by healing feats, allowing it to be countered by some feat combos. 

Also useful in the minion lane to clear or to kill a horde of pikemen, and it is also capable of damaging the ram slightly.

feats.name: Stalwart Banner
feats.description:
Place a banner which persists until the 20 second duration is over, creating an 8m AOE around it where all allies continuously regain health totaling 84 over 20 seconds. 

This also cleanses fire and bleed.
feats.explanation:
The health recovery from Stalwart Banner is not particularly fast, but it can still make a difference in a group fight, and can impact the match outcome if used whilst breaking. 

The heal tends to provoke aggression from your opponents, which can be exploited. Clearing bleed and fire damage can completely neuter some characters if they attack in range of the banner, and counters some feats like Sharpen Blade and Fire Flask. 

Depending on your team's T4 picks, it can be beneficial to pick this feat over another damage-dealing feat. 

In Breach, it is a very strong choice due to the scarcity of healing, and because it can also heal the Commander - although be sure to use it when there are no Pikemen around to distract his AI.

feats.name: Slippery
feats.description:
A joke feat that automatically counters guard breaks, if it were possible to manually counter them (guaranteed GBs in vulnerable frames are not stopped). 

Lasts for 30 seconds. Use this if you find pressing counter guardbreak too difficult.
feats.explanation:
Easily the worst feat in the game, and an utter waste of a Tier 4. You should be able to counter all non-guaranteed GBs easily, so this feat provides nothing useful. Why the devs thought to also give it to Shaolin, I have no idea. 

Recently buffed to not be GB vulnerable during activation, this pathetic buff does nothing to elevate this feat from it's current joke-tier uselessness.

If an enemy is foolish enough to attack you whilst you have Juggernaut active, you can GB them in their attack recovery much like Shugoki's old passive superarmour, or punish them with an attack. 

With most characters nowadays having good gap-closers, rolling away from an opponent who has popped juggernaut is not always an option - unless you are facing Lawbringer or Conqueror.

Passive | Regenerate 15 health every 2 seconds. 

Must be out of guard, and not out of stamina, not sprinting, attacking or any other action, in order to start recovery. 

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.
feats.explanation:
An underwhelming feat that essentially requires you to not be playing the game in order to get any benefit from it - but does give a big benefit when it is active. 

The only things you can do whilst regenerating, are standing still, or walking. Even sprinting, or climbing a ladder, stops regeneration, so you cannot heal during rotations, unless walking rather than sprinting.

feats.explanation:
Easy to hide near the entrance to a zone or in minions to give you an initial advantage if an opponent triggers it, and the stagger can be enough to guarantee a fast attack. Decent AOE and small size makes it hard to avoid. 

The small amout of damage can even kill a low health opponent looking to back-cap a point. 

In Breach, less useful due to a larger map size and more objectives to account for.

feats.name: Executioner's Respite
feats.explanation:
Grants a minimal amount of extra healing from an execution, which is often useless if you are executing on an owned point, or have the Devourer perk active. 

You will only rarely get any value from this feat, so most characters have a stronger T2 available.

feats.name: Doom Banner
feats.description:
Place a stationary banner that creates an 8 meter AOE thats debuffs enemy defense by 25%, and persists after your death. 30 second duration.

Anomalously, Berserker has 966ms activation time, and 1033ms recovery time compared to the listed values of others.
feats.explanation:
The defence debuff that Doom Banner causes is very significant and enough to influence the outcome of a team fight. 

Clever placement near a choke point can ensure that the enemy team are all affected. 

The banner persists and can help your team after you die, and combined with the decent cooldown, means you do not have to worry about wasting its use if you are at low health.

Useful for killing low health players holding onto revenge, ledging opponents, dealing with players trying to disengage (a problem for zerk), and because of the speed, even interrupting enemy punishes on your allies. 

The other Tier 3 feats at your disposal are also pretty good, so it is a tough choice between them all.

feats.name: Sharpen Blade
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, inflict 10 bleed damage (in 2 ticks of 5) on each hit.

Always has 1500ms total use duration (start-up + recovery time), but start up varies per-character. 

Shinobi/Peacekeeper have a 300ms startup. 
Centurion/Orochi/Valkyrie have a 500ms startup. 
Berserker/Aramusha have a 600ms startup.
Nobushi has a 700ms startup.
feats.explanation:
Significantly diminished from its pre-nerf state, if you can look past the very long cooldown, this feat can still give a nice boost to your damage. 

Multi-hit, or fast chain attacks only apply the bleed damage twice in a short interval. Suffers from being negated by Second Wind. Still powerful with a Shaman teammate.

feats.name: Fear Itself
feats.description: Enemies around you take 40% more damage. 8 meter AOE that moves around with you and lasts for 20 seconds.

feats.name: Rush
feats.description: For 10 seconds, your sprint speed is boosted by 30%.

feats.name: Deadly
feats.description: Passive | After a successful attack, you gain a temporary 15% attack bonus for 3 seconds.

feats.name: Bounty Hunter
feats.description: Passive | Gain 16 Health & full Stamina when you kill another Hero.

feats.name: Bloodlust
feats.description: Passive | Killing heroes grants a 20% attack boost, and 20% damage reduction, for 10 seconds.

feats.name: Bear Trap

feats.name: Juggernaut

feats.explanation:
If an enemy is foolish enough to attack you whilst you have Juggernaut active, you can GB them in their attack recovery much like Shugoki's old passive superarmour, or punish them with an attack. 

With most characters nowadays having good gap-closers, rolling away from an opponent who has popped juggernaut is not always an option - unless you are facing Lawbringer or Conqueror.

feats.name: Javelin
feats.description: Throw a javelin for 40 damage.

feats.name: Fury
feats.description: For 20 seconds, Raise sprint speed by 15%, attack by 20% and gain 20% damage reduction.

Centurion/Orochi/Valkyrie have a 500ms startup. 
Berserker/Aramusha have a 600ms startup.
Nobushi has a 700ms startup.

Significantly diminished from its pre-nerf state, if you can look past the very long cooldown, this feat can still give a nice boost to your damage.

feats.name: Scout

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.

feats.name: Hamarr's Favor
feats.description: Passive | Gain a 20 health shield that stacks and lasts forever after landing Hamarr Slam on an enemy.
feats.explanation:

feats.description: Gain unlimited stamina for 15 seconds.

feats.name: Righteous Deflection
feats.description: Passive | 50% damage reduction after parrying, for 5 seconds.
feats.explanation: Halving incoming damage for 5 seconds after a parry can be rather useful when stalling in a gank situation, particularly against ganks that are set up from a parry, like Shaman's Bite.

feats.name: Zealot's Bolt
feats.description:
Throw a hammer that deals 25 damage, and drains all the opponent's stamina. 

The projectile can wallsplat an opponent, or knock them into a hazard.
feats.explanation:
The obvious visual and sound cues on start up, make this feat pretty easy to dodge on reaction, which limits its usefullness. 

Additionally it feeds a lot of revenge (counteracting the entire OOS effect), and can put a teammate out of stamina if it hits them, so careless use of it will actively harm your team. 

However, in certain circumstances it can do good damage if you wallsplat with it to guarantee forward dodge heavy. Also remember if the opponent is Out-of-Lock when hit by the Hamarr, and they are wallsplatted, the OOL state persists throughout their stagger, allowing for a full OOL OOS punish and enormous damage. Check the punishes table to see those punishes.

feats.name: Punch Through
feats.description: Passive | Doubles block damage. (From 18% to 36%)
feats.explanation: Blocked attacks do a bit more damage with this feat active, although still feed a lot of revenge. Chip damage cannot kill, so you still need to land a hit to finish off turtles. Overrides any other damage buffs that would otherwise affect chip damage.

feats.name: Hard to Kill
feats.description: Passive | Gain 30% damage reduction when below 50 health.
feats.explanation:

The effective health increase from this feat is only 15HP, at the most, but due to the way that damage is calculated, you will rarely even reach this low maximum as you will not gain damage reduction from the attack that brings you below 50 health. 

It also has terrible synergy with other feats and perks, as damage reduction does not stack. Last Stand is typically better, and doesn't require you to give up a T3 option.

feats.name: Twilight of the Gods
feats.description:
Slam your Hamarr on the ground, taking 1500ms, with hyperarmour. 

Does 25 damage and knocks down all opponents within a 8 meter AOE centred 1 meter in front of the Jormungandr.
feats.explanation:
A slow start-up makes this feat fairly easy to avoid, but it is still often possible to hit multiple opponents, guaranteeing a Hamarr Slam on one of them. However, it is comparatively easy to interrupt with a fast bash, limiting it's use for anti-ganking.
