Stronger than Inspire due to not being avoidable or lost on death, though can be used improperly on an injured target.

feats.name: Inspire
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, you and your allies within a 10 meter AOE deal 20% more damage. 

This also causes the soldiers near you to fight faster and sprint forward.
feats.explanation:
A good damage buff, with a decent duration, that can give a significant advantage to your team in a team fight. The fairly quick cooldown allows you to use it without hesitation. 

In Breach, it gains another level of utility as the damage and attack speed boost also applies to pikemen. 

As a defender, this can be used to do huge damage to the ram, and for both teams it can make a crowd of allied pikemen far more lethal.

feats.name: Smoke Bomb
feats.description: Throw a smoke bomb on the ground that stuns and blinds opponents for 5 seconds, removing their attack indicators.
feats.explanation: A feat that is typically outclassed by the other options in the slot, as T2 feats are generally strong - if you dislike the other options, this is still a choice if you are a character with a decent roll catcher, or for a free GB, as people tend to roll/dodge out of the smoke. It makes attacking people easier, but is just a stun effect, so the feat is inconsistent depending on who you use it against.

feats.name: Longbow
feats.description: Fire a long bow for 40 Damage.
feats.explanation:
As a projectile feat, Longbow can be useful to kill opponents holding onto revenge, or interrupt distant revives or executions. 

It does a great chunk of damage, which is easily confirmed by an ally, making it useful for ganks, and with standardisation of speed to 700ms, can be used more easily in some 1v1 scenarios.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow. 

The feat can almost completely negate damage over time feats like Nail Bomb or Fire Flask, or punishes from bleed-based characters. 

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Steadfast
feats.description:
Enemy throw attempts do not work for 30 seconds after activation. 

Also prevents Stampede Charge and Crashing Charge from affecting you.
feats.explanation: Pretty much pointless as the opponent can still get a regular GB punish on you, and you have to activate it in anticipation of being thrown. Potentially has some use if you are facing a team with multiple Raiders or Warlords due to negating Stampede and Crashing Charge, but otherwise a terrible choice.

feats.name: Arrow Storm
feats.description:
5 waves of 50 damage arrow showers over a 15 meter AOE. 

First wave takes 1100ms to land, with each subsequent wave taking another 1300ms. 

Can only be used outside.
feats.explanation:
It can be hard to hit aware opponents with this feat, as it can be fairly easily avoided, unless they are engaged by allies. 

The large AOE makes it great for clearing mid, and it can kill a lot of pikemen, and do very good damage to the ram. One wave of arrows is rarely enough to kill an opponent, and the feat also does considerable friendly fire damage. 

However, with careful targeting it is still capable of wiping an entire team if they are badly positioned.

feats.name: Unblockable
feats.description: For 20 seconds, all your attacks are unblockable.
feats.explanation:
This feat is unsurprisingly very powerful, giving Kensei an almost overwhelming offence for its duration. In a 1v1 scenario, Kensei's 500ms lights and the recent changes to indicators makes this feat pretty scary. Opponents will often disengage and flee from a Kensei with this feat active. 

In a team fight can make Kensei's sweeping off-target heavies, zone and dodge attacks almost impossible to avoid, making him very dangerous, especially combined with Chilling Stare or Inspire.

feats.name: Stalwart Banner
feats.description:
Place a banner which persists until the 20 second duration is over, creating an 8m AOE around it where all allies continuously regain health totaling 84 over 20 seconds. 

This also cleanses fire and bleed.
feats.explanation:
The health recovery from Stalwart Banner is not particularly fast, but it can still make a difference in a group fight, and can impact the match outcome if used whilst breaking. 

The heal tends to provoke aggression from your opponents, which can be exploited. Clearing bleed and fire damage can completely neuter some characters if they attack in range of the banner, and counters some feats like Sharpen Blade and Fire Flask. 

Depending on your team's T4 picks, it can be beneficial to pick this feat over another damage-dealing feat. 

In Breach, it is a very strong choice due to the scarcity of healing, and because it can also heal the Commander - although be sure to use it when there are no Pikemen around to distract his AI.

feats.name: Speed Revive
feats.description: Passive | Revives are 33% faster (ie. take 2.7 seconds instead of 4 seconds).
feats.explanation: A decent feat, can let you revive an ally more easily in a team fight, or with nearby enemy soldiers or pikemen.

feats.name: Iron Lungs
feats.description: Passive | Able to sprint while out of stamina. Recover stamina faster while running.
feats.explanation:
Basically useless. You can regen stamina whilst sprinting without this feat, and the increased rate is hardly noticable. 

Only conceivable use is to allow you to dodge roll without having to stop sprinting if you go OOS, and allowing you to unlock sprint to avoid OOS pressure from certain characters.

feats.name: Throw Farther
feats.description: Passive | Throw Enemies 50% farther‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎
feats.explanation:
Before Shugoki's rework, this had a potential use to help get wallsplats - the only way he could land a Demon's Embrace in a 1v1. 

Now that DE is easier to land, it is less worth taking. It has no effect on Demon Ball, and can make you miss your OOS punishes, making it detrimental in some situations. 

However, it can allow you to get environmental kills where you otherwise would not, giving it some utility - and his other T1s are underhwelming, so it can be worth taking if you feel like it.

feats.name: Short Tempered
feats.description: Passive | Deal 20% more damage for 5 seconds after taking damage.
feats.explanation:
This is a considerable attack buff that can be frequently available, but does rely on taking damage to be used, making it rather reliant on the character's kit. 

Additionally, doesn't match up to the power of Juggernaut, which is a far better choice in general.

For 10 Seconds, your movement speed is slowed and you cannot sprint. 20% damage reduction, auto counter guard break, uninterruptible.

Anomalously, Lawbringer and Warlord have 100ms and 800ms recoveries respectively, compared to the 600ms of others.
feats.explanation:
If an enemy is foolish enough to attack you whilst you have Juggernaut active, you can GB them in their attack recovery much like Shugoki's old passive superarmour, or punish them with an attack. 

With most characters nowadays having good gap-closers, rolling away from an opponent who has popped juggernaut is not always an option - unless you are facing Lawbringer or Conqueror. 

Due to the nerfed damage reduction, this feat no longer makes you nigh unkillable, so care must be taken to activate it whilst you have enough health to trade with. It still has good utility to stall in a zone, prevent a coordinated gank, or to disrupt in mid when the opponent is forced to engage or else lose the point.

It is far less useful in Breach, where stalling objectives is less important. However it does let you get a revive or execution uninterrupted by pikemen, which can be useful.

feats.name: Punch Through
feats.description: Passive | Doubles block damage. (From 18% to 36%)
feats.explanation: Blocked attacks do a bit more damage with this feat active, although still feed a lot of revenge. Chip damage cannot kill, so you still need to land a hit to finish off turtles. Overrides any other damage buffs that would otherwise affect chip damage.

feats.description: Passive | Gain 30% damage reduction when below 50 health.
feats.explanation:
Whilst this feat may seem useful at first glance, on closer inspection it is very underwhelming. The effective health increase from this feat is only 15HP, at the most, but due to the way that damage is calculated, you will rarely even reach this low maximum as you will not gain damage reduction from the attack that brings you below 50 health. 

It also has terrible synergy with other feats and perks, as damage reduction does not stack. Last Stand is typically better, and doesn't require you to give up a T3 option.

feats.name: Staggering Blows
feats.description: For 20 seconds, Any successful heavy will also knock the foe down. Throws will also knockdown the opponent. Also knocks down allies.
feats.explanation:
Despite having the significant disadvantage of knocking down your own teammates, with Shugoki's reworks, this feat has become one of the most powerful in the game. 

Shugoki's heavies and zone land rather more easily now, and with an ally, you can get guaranteed knockdown from even a countered GB, making him a lethal ganker with this feat active. 

A max charged heavy is normally guaranteed on any unbalanced opponent for big damage, as well as an ally attack. A very long duration, and a fairly subtle effect on Shugoki's club, are other advantages to this feat.

Passive | Regenerate 15 health every 2 seconds. 

Must be out of guard, and not out of stamina, not sprinting, attacking or any other action, in order to start recovery. 

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.
feats.explanation:
An underwhelming feat that essentially requires you to not be playing the game in order to get any benefit from it - but does give a big benefit when it is active. 

The only things you can do whilst regenerating, are standing still, or walking. Even sprinting, or climbing a ladder, stops regeneration, so you cannot heal during rotations, unless walking rather than sprinting. 

Can have a niche use to regen health by unlocking at the edge of team fights, and is overall better now that the healing rate of capture zones has been reduced making it worth taking if you lack any better T4s. 

More useful in Breach, where you can walk forward with the ram, (or let it push you), or in Tribute when guarding an offering. But even then, a Tier 4 takes a long time to unlock, so you won't have much time to make use of it.

Shinobi/Peacekeeper have a 300ms startup. 
Centurion/Orochi/Valkyrie have a 500ms startup.

Nobushi has a 700ms startup.

feats.name: Nail Bomb

In Breach, can be used effectively to kill anyone entering the healing zone, or give a nasty surprise to an enemy trying to activate the caudron, use the ballista, etc

May allow you to clear a bit more before having to head to the heal zone, but many other Tier 1s are superior in this mode.

In Breach, can be used effectively to kill anyone entering the healing zone, or give a nasty surprise to an enemy trying to activate the caudron, use the ballista, etc

feats.name: Yama Uba
feats.description:
Passive | Heal 20% of damage dealt when you damage your opponent. 

Can be used on soldiers. Works with bleed.
feats.explanation:
Since the nerf, this feat provides a small amount of healing that procs on sharpened hits, minions, and feats, but in practice doesn't swing 1v1s hugely in your favour much any more. 

Can heal you under a revenge shield, which gives you more survivability in ganks..

feats.name: Iron Lungs
feats.description: Passive | Able to sprint while out of stamina. Recover stamina faster while running.
feats.explanation:
Basically useless. You can regen stamina whilst sprinting without this feat, and the increased rate is hardly noticable. 

Only conceivable use is to allow you to dodge roll without having to stop sprinting if you go OOS, and allowing you to unlock sprint to avoid OOS pressure from certain characters.

feats.name: Body Count
feats.description: Passive | Killing a soldier or pikeman through any means (including feats) grants you 1 health and 1 stamina.
feats.explanation:
A decent pick for mid lane characters in Dominion, this feat allows for some sustain whilst clearing minions, but is no longer really enough to stay in mid indefinitely. 

In Breach, this feat is extremely underwhelming, as you have to kill 10 pikemen to heal a single poke's worth of damage. 

May allow you to clear a bit more before having to head to the heal zone, but many other Tier 1s are superior in this mode.

feats.name: Deadly
feats.description: Passive | After a successful attack, you gain a temporary 15% attack bonus for 3 seconds.
feats.explanation: The damage boost is only triggered on landed attacks, and isn't triggered by chip damage or by landing a bash, or guard break - however, with the improved openers on characters that have been reworked, and the CCU making attacks land more consistently across the board, this feat can give a fairly reliable damage buff, especially on high damage chain attacks.

feats.name: Smoke Bomb
feats.description: Throw a smoke bomb on the ground that stuns and blinds opponents for 5 seconds, removing their attack indicators.
feats.explanation: A feat that is typically outclassed by the other options in the slot, as T2 feats are generally strong - if you dislike the other options, this is still a choice if you are a character with a decent roll catcher, or for a free GB, as people tend to roll/dodge out of the smoke. It makes attacking people easier, but is just a stun effect, so the feat is inconsistent depending on who you use it against.

feats.name: Juggernaut
feats.description:
For 10 Seconds, your movement speed is slowed and you cannot sprint. 20% damage reduction, auto counter guard break, uninterruptible.

Anomalously, Lawbringer and Warlord have 100ms and 800ms recoveries respectively, compared to the 600ms of others.
feats.explanation:
If an enemy is foolish enough to attack you whilst you have Juggernaut active, you can GB them in their attack recovery much like Shugoki's old passive superarmour, or punish them with an attack. 

With most characters nowadays having good gap-closers, rolling away from an opponent who has popped juggernaut is not always an option - unless you are facing Lawbringer or Conqueror. 

Due to the nerfed damage reduction, this feat no longer makes you nigh unkillable, so care must be taken to activate it whilst you have enough health to trade with. It still has good utility to stall in a zone, prevent a coordinated gank, or to disrupt in mid when the opponent is forced to engage or else lose the point.

It is far less useful in Breach, where stalling objectives is less important. However it does let you get a revive or execution uninterrupted by pikemen, which can be useful.

feats.name: Short Tempered
feats.description: Passive | Deal 20% more damage for 5 seconds after taking damage.
feats.explanation:
This is a considerable attack buff that can be frequently available, but does rely on taking damage to be used, making it rather reliant on the character's kit. 

Additionally, doesn't match up to the power of Juggernaut, which is a far better choice in general.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow. 

The feat can almost completely negate damage over time feats like Nail Bomb or Fire Flask, or punishes from bleed-based characters. 

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Sharpen Blade
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, inflict 10 bleed damage (in 2 ticks of 5) on each hit.

Always has 1500ms total use duration (start-up + recovery time), but start up varies per-character. 

Shinobi/Peacekeeper have a 300ms startup. 
Centurion/Orochi/Valkyrie have a 500ms startup. 
Berserker/Aramusha have a 600ms startup.
Nobushi has a 700ms startup.
feats.explanation:
Significantly diminished from its pre-nerf state, if you can look past the very long cooldown, this feat can still give a nice boost to your damage. 

Multi-hit, or fast chain attacks only apply the bleed damage twice in a short interval. Suffers from being negated by Second Wind. Still powerful with a Shaman teammate.

feats.name: Flaming Arrow
feats.description: Fire a flaming arrow for 10 physical and 40 fire damage.
feats.explanation:
In theory this feat does 10 damage more than Longbow, but in practice, the fire damage can be completely negated by healing feats, or being in a zone. 

It does do full damage despite damage reduction, so that's nice.

feats.name: Arrow Storm
feats.description:
5 waves of 50 damage arrow showers over a 15 meter AOE. 

First wave takes 1100ms to land, with each subsequent wave taking another 1300ms. 

Can only be used outside.
feats.explanation:
It can be hard to hit aware opponents with this feat, as it can be fairly easily avoided, unless they are engaged by allies. 

The large AOE makes it great for clearing mid, and it can kill a lot of pikemen, and do very good damage to the ram. One wave of arrows is rarely enough to kill an opponent, and the feat also does considerable friendly fire damage. 

However, with careful targeting it is still capable of wiping an entire team if they are badly positioned.

feats.name: Stalwart Banner
feats.description:
Place a banner which persists until the 20 second duration is over, creating an 8m AOE around it where all allies continuously regain health totaling 84 over 20 seconds. 

This also cleanses fire and bleed.
feats.explanation:
The health recovery from Stalwart Banner is not particularly fast, but it can still make a difference in a group fight, and can impact the match outcome if used whilst breaking. 

The heal tends to provoke aggression from your opponents, which can be exploited. Clearing bleed and fire damage can completely neuter some characters if they attack in range of the banner, and counters some feats like Sharpen Blade and Fire Flask. 

Depending on your team's T4 picks, it can be beneficial to pick this feat over another damage-dealing feat. 

In Breach, it is a very strong choice due to the scarcity of healing, and because it can also heal the Commander - although be sure to use it when there are no Pikemen around to distract his AI.

feats.name: Fear Itself
feats.description: Enemies around you take 40% more damage. 8 meter AOE that moves around with you and lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation: A good Tier 4 feat that can give your team a big advantage in a team fight, and can help anti-gank as well. Has great synergy with any feat that buffs damage.

feats.name: Deliverance
feats.description:
Passive | Executions cannot be interrupted by regular attacks or attacks from soldiers or pikemen. GB, bashes, and feats can interrupt still. 

Applies a 120 health shield during the execution.
feats.explanation:
Hitokiri gets executions comparatively easily and whilst executions with this feat are not truly "uninterruptible" as a knowledgeable opponent can GB or bash you out of one, in practice it allows you to execute opponents with impunity. 

Especially useful in mid or surrounded by pikemen, and even in team fights or being ganked - where you can greatly benefit from the healing and preventing revives.

Useful in Breach due to the scarcity of healing - the ability to heal in the midst of the pikemen is not to be undervalued.

feats.name: Iron Lungs
feats.description: Passive | Able to sprint while out of stamina. Recover stamina faster while running.
feats.explanation:
Basically useless. You can regen stamina whilst sprinting without this feat, and the increased rate is hardly noticable. 

Only conceivable use is to allow you to dodge roll without having to stop sprinting if you go OOS, and allowing you to unlock sprint to avoid OOS pressure from certain characters.

feats.name: Fast Recovery
feats.description: Passive | Stamina regenerates twice as fast. Also works when exhausted.
feats.explanation: Allows you to be a bit more aggressive with stamina-intensive attacks, and escape OOS state much faster. Also useful for zoning more frequently in mid lane or team fights. If you take this feat, there is no need to bother with the Fresh Focus perk.

feats.name: Tainted Gift
feats.description:
Marks an opponent - If you or an ally executes this opponent within 30 seconds, the executioner, and any allies within a 12 meter AOE are healed 50 health. 

Adds to the healing of the execution, and does not cleanse bleed.
feats.explanation:
Heals your allies a large amount, and can practically heal the executioner to full if a longer execution is used. 

Excellent synergy with Hitokiri's uninterruptible executions, and a decent cooldown allows this feat to be used to great effect in a team fight, although is somewhat situational. 

Better in Breach due to the scarcity of healing, allowing your team to stay longer on the ramparts or by the ram, and it also works on Captains.

feats.name: Bloodlust
feats.description: Passive | Killing heroes grants a 20% attack boost, and 20% damage reduction, for 10 seconds.
feats.explanation: This is a signficant temporary attack and defence boost, which can really help in both anti-gank and team-fight scenarios.

feats.name: Righteous Deflection
feats.description: Passive | 50% damage reduction after parrying, for 5 seconds.
feats.explanation: Halving incoming damage for 5 seconds after a parry can be rather useful when stalling in a gank situation, particularly against ganks that are set up from a parry, like Shaman's Bite.

feats.name: Spirit Shroud
feats.description: Passive | After executing an opponent, gain 25% damage reduction, that lasts until your death.
feats.explanation:
The damage reduction on this feat is really nice, and synergises with Hitokiri's playstyle of wanting to trade - though it requires you to get an execution first.

Still might not be worth taking over Nukekubi, which allows for infinite offense.

feats.name: Heal on Block
feats.description: Passive | Blocking regenerates 4 Health.
feats.explanation:
The usefulness of this feat is fairly self-explanatory, and can discourage opponents from attacking you in a 1v1. 

Can also help survivabilty in ganks, as you can heal under the revenge shield. However, in practice, you still will take some chip damage from heavy attacks, and most competent opponents won't be throwing easily blockable lights anyway. 

No longer heals from minion or pikemen attacks, which removes its previous strength in mid.

feats.name: Nukekubi
feats.description:
Passive | Regenerate stamina on successful attacks or bashes. 

Also triggers on any feat that causes hitstun, like projectile feats, and can be used on soldiers. 

Stamina gained seems related to the stagger of the attack, and is normally enough to recoup the entire cost of regular attacks, and some bashes.
feats.explanation: The gained from this feat can be fairly substantial, although it doesn't work on blocked attacks. Still slightly underwhelming for a tier 3, as it rather selfish, but can allow for continuous offence if successful. Works on minions and can allow for efficient mid clearing.

feats.name: Senbonzakura
feats.description:
Launch a 1700ms, unblockable, parriable, but unfeintable, top attack at an opponent, dealing 200 damage, and executing on kill. 

Can be dodged, and has regular hyperarmour throughout (ie. bashes + feats interrupt). 

Feat can be reused without a cooldown if interrupted.
feats.explanation:
Trivial to dodge or parry if used on a lone opponent, this executing one-shot feat is only usable with an ally to confirm it with hitstun or a GB, where it becomes an instakill gank. Can also be guaranteed off an OOS or revenge knockdown. 

Currently, it can also kill multiple opponents from one use, either if two opponents are standing close together, or if it hits an off-target foe, as it will count as an interrupt and be able to be used again without the cooldown activating. 

In Breach, it does huge damage to the commander, especially with damage buffs applied.

feats.name: Regenerate
feats.description:
Passive | Regenerate 15 health every 2 seconds. 

Must be out of guard, and not out of stamina, not sprinting, attacking or any other action, in order to start recovery. 

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.
feats.explanation:
An underwhelming feat that essentially requires you to not be playing the game in order to get any benefit from it - but does give a big benefit when it is active. 

The only things you can do whilst regenerating, are standing still, or walking. Even sprinting, or climbing a ladder, stops regeneration, so you cannot heal during rotations, unless walking rather than sprinting. 

Can have a niche use to regen health by unlocking at the edge of team fights, and is overall better now that the healing rate of capture zones has been reduced making it worth taking if you lack any better T4s. 

More useful in Breach, where you can walk forward with the ram, (or let it push you), or in Tribute when guarding an offering. But even then, a Tier 4 takes a long time to unlock, so you won't have much time to make use of it.

feats.name: Fear Itself
feats.description: Enemies around you take 40% more damage. 8 meter AOE that moves around with you and lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation: A good Tier 4 feat that can give your team a big advantage in a team fight, and can help anti-gank as well. Has great synergy with any feat that buffs damage.

feats.name: Kagerou
feats.description:
Passive | For 10 seconds after superior blocking an incoming attack, each of your attacks does an additional 3 bleed damage.

Active duration is reset upon subsequent superior blocks.
feats.explanation:
Adds a good amount of damage to Kyoshin's punishes, which can help compensate for their otherwise fairly low damage. 

More effective on the Kaze Stance follow up Fujin Cuts, due to adding a flat amount of bleed per hit. 

Good synergy with Nobushi, PK, and Shaman. Considering Kyoshin's sub-par alternate T1 choices, this is definitely worth taking.

feats.name: Iron Lungs
feats.description: Passive | Able to sprint while out of stamina. Recover stamina faster while running.
feats.explanation:
Basically useless. You can regen stamina whilst sprinting without this feat, and the increased rate is hardly noticable. 

Only conceivable use is to allow you to dodge roll without having to stop sprinting if you go OOS, and allowing you to unlock sprint to avoid OOS pressure from certain characters.

feats.name: Speed Revive
feats.description: Passive | Revives are 33% faster (ie. take 2.7 seconds instead of 4 seconds).
feats.explanation: A decent feat, can let you revive an ally more easily in a team fight, or with nearby enemy soldiers or pikemen.

feats.name: Hikarimore
feats.description:
Passive | For 10 seconds after superior blocking an incoming attack, heal 3 hp per attack you land on an opponent.

Active duration is reset upon subsequent superior blocks.
feats.explanation:
The heal per attack on superior block is decent, but lower than comparable self-heal moves. It gives much more value on Kaze Stance attacks and their follow-ups due to healing a flat amount per hit. 

With both T1 and T2 active, the full block counters have more than double the health swing, making them very strong - if you can get the hits off without being interrupted in team fights that is...

feats.name: Arrow Strike
feats.description: Call a 45 damage arrow strike within a 6 meter AOE. Only works outside.
feats.explanation:
Slow speed can make it hard to hit with unless an ally confirms it, but it does good damage and has a fast cooldown. 

More useful in Breach where it can quickly kill a crowd of pikemen. Can no longer be i-framed, so is now consistent with all other AOE feats.

feats.name: Smoke Bomb
feats.description: Throw a smoke bomb on the ground that stuns and blinds opponents for 5 seconds, removing their attack indicators.
feats.explanation: A feat that is typically outclassed by the other options in the slot, as T2 feats are generally strong - if you dislike the other options, this is still a choice if you are a character with a decent roll catcher, or for a free GB, as people tend to roll/dodge out of the smoke. It makes attacking people easier, but is just a stun effect, so the feat is inconsistent depending on who you use it against.

feats.name: Hikari To Kage
feats.description:
For 10 seconds both your unique T1 and T2 are activated, even if you do not have them equipped.

Upon superior blocking an incoming attack, regenerate X stamina, and the feat's active duration is reset.
feats.explanation:
Compared to other tier 3 feats, this is rather an underwhelming feat. It only benefits the Kyoshin, compared to other feats which benefit the whole team, and the buff duration is very short, despite a short cooldown. 

However, Kyoshin sadly lacks other strong T3 choices, so taking it is not a huge loss of potential.

It does allow for you to run arrow strike instead of the healing feat and still get value out of the healing, though Tough as Nails and the unique T2 is also a decent combo.

feats.name: Tough as Nails
feats.description:
Passive | Raises max Health by 15% but does not heal when first unlocked. 

Subsequent respawns will give you full health (Except in Elimination).
feats.explanation:
More health is always nice. Combined with the Bulk Up and Bastion perks, can make you quite tanky and hard to dislodge from a capture point. It doesn't effect the amount of revenge build up you need to activate revenge, making stalling easier in comparison. 

Don't use it in Elimination, where for some reason, it doesn't work on respawn.

feats.name: Protected Revive
feats.description: Passive | Grants a 75 health overshield to revived allies, which lasts for 15 seconds.
feats.explanation: Removal of hyperarmour from this feat means it no longer allows easier revives in mid or in team fights. Not only does this feat rely on you getting revives, your ally also has to be in combat within 15s of being revived to receive any benefit, making this feat so situational that it is basically useless.

feats.name: Mugen Houyou
feats.description:
Summon pinning spikes on all opponents within an X meter AOE centered on the Kyoshin. 

Spikes have an ~4 meter AOE centred on each opponent in range, and take 1366ms to hit. 

On hit, spikes do 25 damage, and pin the opponent in place for 2200ms, or until hit. 1100ms activation animation. Spikes do friendly fire damage to allies, but will only pin opponents.
feats.explanation:
An okay Tier 4, which can lead to good team synergy, as it can facilitate a lot of extra damage with teammates. 

The damage AOEs are rather slow to land, and can easily be avoided if opponents are paying attention, so using it in an anti-gank situation is rarely optimal. Despite a slow time to hit, the activation is fast, so it is hard for opponents to interrupt. 

Optimally it will be used it in team fights where opponents are in recoveries or block/hitstun, and grouped up to land it more reliably, and with allies to add damage from attacks or their own powerful feats. As it cannot pin yourself or allies, it is relatively safe to use even if you will do friendly fire - but be careful not to kill low health allies or yourself!

feats.name: Arrow Storm
feats.description:
5 waves of 50 damage arrow showers over a 15 meter AOE. 

First wave takes 1100ms to land, with each subsequent wave taking another 1300ms. 

Can only be used outside.
feats.explanation:
It can be hard to hit aware opponents with this feat, as it can be fairly easily avoided, unless they are engaged by allies. 

The large AOE makes it great for clearing mid, and it can kill a lot of pikemen, and do very good damage to the ram. One wave of arrows is rarely enough to kill an opponent, and the feat also does considerable friendly fire damage. 

However, with careful targeting it is still capable of wiping an entire team if they are badly positioned.

feats.name: Fear Itself
feats.description: Enemies around you take 40% more damage. 8 meter AOE that moves around with you and lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation: A good Tier 4 feat that can give your team a big advantage in a team fight, and can help anti-gank as well. Has great synergy with any feat that buffs damage.

feats.name: Rally Call
feats.description: Passive | When under 50 Health, allies within a 15 meter AOE gain 15% damage boost for 5 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Now actually works, and gives your team a good damage boost whenever you are at low health. 

To get the most use, you will have to stay near the edge of team fights and stay alive whilst at low health, but it is still generically useful as there are always going to be some fights where you are at low health. 

Great synergy with Tiandi's T3 and T4 unique feats that increase surviveability whilst at lower health.

feats.name: Come at Me
feats.description: For 30 seconds, you gain 50% more renown and gain 20hp on hero kill, but you take 20% more damage.
feats.explanation: Can be used in the minion lane greatly increasing your renown gain for killing soldiers. Allows you to reach your higher tier feats very quickly. In Breach, using this just before killing the Guardian will give you a huge amount of renown.

feats.name: Tireless
feats.description: Passive | Actions use 17% less stamina.
feats.explanation:
Allows you to attack a bit more frequently, but not all that impressive.

Note: Does not stack with the perk: endurance.

feats.name: Sacrifice
feats.description:
Sacrifice 49 heath to heal 30 health over 24 seconds, and fully restore stamina to allies within a 21 meter AOE. 

Clears bleed or fire damage for the duration of the heal. Tiandi also gains full stamina.

Re-casting the feat within its 24 second active window will not refresh its active timer to those previously affected by it.
feats.explanation:
Whilst in theory, sacrificing 50 of your own health to heal 30 health to each of your allies is a worthy trade-off, in practice a scenario where you can take advantage of this rarely occurs, and the heal is so slow as to be barely noticable. 

Potentially synergises well with Tier 3 Vital Leech to regain lost health. Needs a very well coordinated team to make use of. 

The immunity to bleed and fire damage whilst this feat is active is far more useful than the heal itself, giving it a niche use to counter some AOE feats like Fire Flask.

feats.name: Marked For Death
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, target's position is revealed on the map for all allies and their defense is lowered by 15% and attacks take 25% more stamina. 

You also receive 50% more renown on their death (assists count as well).

Can be negated by Stealth.
feats.explanation:
A decent debuff that can swing a 1v1 or help get rid of a troublesome opponent in a team fight. Long cooldown and fairly short duration is the biggest drawback. 

This feat is completely negated by stealth, so do NOT use it on a hero with stealth.

feats.name: Doom Banner
feats.description:
Place a stationary banner that creates an 8 meter AOE thats debuffs enemy defense by 25%, and persists after your death. 30 second duration.

Anomalously, Berserker has 966ms activation time, and 1033ms recovery time compared to the listed values of others.
feats.explanation:
The defence debuff that Doom Banner causes is very significant and enough to influence the outcome of a team fight. 

Clever placement near a choke point can ensure that the enemy team are all affected. 

The banner persists and can help your team after you die, and combined with the decent cooldown, means you do not have to worry about wasting its use if you are at low health.

feats.name: Vital Leech
feats.description: Passive | Whilst below 50 health, heal 35% of damage dealt to opponents.
feats.explanation:
Combined with your Tier 4 Indomitable, this feat can give Tiandi a fair amount of sustain, especially because it can heal you underneath a shield. Triggering off soldiers and pikemen gives valuable healing in Breach Mode, where it is much better. 

In a coordinated dominon team, Battlecry might be a better choice.

feats.name: Battlecry
feats.description:
On activation, causes all enemy soldiers within a 21 meter AOE to flee. 

All allies across the map gain a 25% attack damage boost that lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Can give your entire team a good damage boost to turn a team fight in your favour. The soldier fleeing effect super useful too, as it essentially gives you a free cap on the mid lane, and enables easier executions and revives there. 

In Breach it is useful for the damage boost in a team fight or when attacking the Commander, but for some reason the fleeing effect does not work on Pikemen or Archers, reducing its utility.

feats.name: Protected Revive
feats.description: Passive | Grants a 75 health overshield to revived allies, which lasts for 15 seconds.
feats.explanation: Removal of hyperarmour from this feat means it no longer allows easier revives in mid or in team fights. Not only does this feat rely on you getting revives, your ally also has to be in combat within 15s of being revived to receive any benefit, making this feat so situational that it is basically useless.

feats.name: Indomitable
feats.description:
Passive | Gain a 50 health shield for 15 seconds when below 25 health. 

Bleed, Sacrifice and Chip Damage does not trigger the feat, a successful opponent attack/feat has to land.

The 90 second cooldown is reset when you reach 70 HP, though the UI does not show this if the 90s CD is already triggered.
feats.explanation:
Gives significantly improved ability to survive in a team fight or makes you into a stall monster if the opponents think about ganking you, especially if you're able to proc the reset condition of 70 health with healing from feats like Vital Leech or Thrilling Comeback.

Be careful not to be hit by an attack that kills you before reaching critical health, as the feat will not trigger that way. Neither will it trigger from bleed, chip damage, or sacrifice, so plan accordingly.

feats.name: Morale Booster
feats.description: Boosts the damage of you and all of your allies on the map by 30% for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A feat that gives a good damage boost to your entire team, regardless of where they are on the map. The 20s duration requires intelligent use, but it can be instrumental to finish off a breaking team without a chance for them to rally - especially because it boosts ally feat damage. 

As well as team fights, it can help an ally being ganked before you arrive to help. 

In Breach, it is fantastic for attackers when you get to the commander phase, as the cooldown is short enough to often allow it to be used a second time in the phase if necessary, and also boosts the damage of an ally on the ballista.

feats.name: Last Laugh
feats.description: Passive | Drop an explosive on death. Cannot activate if executed. Deals 20-100 damage depending on how far the enemy is from the center of the 10 meter AOE.
feats.explanation:
Because this feat requires your death, and can be prevented from working by an execution, it is somewhat underwhelming. 

Ensuring that you don't die prematurely or where the grenade is ineffective (eg. fall damage) can be challenging. But running into a gank, intentionally dying to a light attack, and getting a quad kill is possibly one of the most satisfying moments this game can offer. 

Because the commander's overhead unblockable will not execute, you can easily do great damage to him, and kill any defenders that are clustered nearby.

feats.name: Against All Odds
feats.description: You and allies within an 20 meter AOE deal 5% more damage, gaining an additional +5% per enemy within range (Max 25%) for 10 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Gives a small boost unless all opponents are in range, but can be good in a team fight or anti-gank. 

Has a very short duration, but also a fast recharge speed to compensate. 

Be wary that it leaves you vulnerable for 1 second to cast it.

feats.name: Deadly
feats.description: Passive | After a successful attack, you gain a temporary 15% attack bonus for 3 seconds.
feats.explanation: The damage boost is only triggered on landed attacks, and isn't triggered by chip damage or by landing a bash, or guard break - however, with the improved openers on characters that have been reworked, and the CCU making attacks land more consistently across the board, this feat can give a fairly reliable damage buff, especially on high damage chain attacks.

feats.name: Speed Revive
feats.description: Passive | Revives are 33% faster (ie. take 2.7 seconds instead of 4 seconds).
feats.explanation: A decent feat, can let you revive an ally more easily in a team fight, or with nearby enemy soldiers or pikemen.

feats.name: Benefaction
feats.description:
Passive | Allies within a 20 meter AOE benefit from Sifu's Poise, regenerating about 35 stamina/second. 

Effect depends on how long the stance is held.
feats.explanation: In theory, can give your allies a lot more stamina in a team fight, but in practice, very hard to coordinate. It is difficult to see when your allies might need more stamina, as JJ it is probably better for you to take a more active role in a team fight, rather than a support role.

feats.name: Inspire
feats.description:
For 20 seconds, you and your allies within a 10 meter AOE deal 20% more damage. 

This also causes the soldiers near you to fight faster and sprint forward.
feats.explanation:
A good damage buff, with a decent duration, that can give a significant advantage to your team in a team fight. The fairly quick cooldown allows you to use it without hesitation. 

In Breach, it gains another level of utility as the damage and attack speed boost also applies to pikemen. 

As a defender, this can be used to do huge damage to the ram, and for both teams it can make a crowd of allied pikemen far more lethal.

feats.name: Executioner's Respite
feats.explanation:
Grants a minimal amount of extra healing from an execution, which is often useless if you are executing on an owned point, or have the Devourer perk active. 

You will only rarely get any value from this feat, so most characters have a stronger T2 available.

feats.name: Soothing Mist
feats.description:
Heals you and any allies in an 18 meter AOE for 10 health, + 5 health for every enemy within range (maximum 30 health with 4 nearby enemies). 

Also clears bleed and fire damage.
feats.explanation:
With nerfs to other healing feats, Soothing Mist is now worth consideration as a source of healing - essentially acting as a full-team Second Wind if you are in a 4v4 teamfight. 

Still a shadow of its former self, this feat is more useful in Breach, where healing is scarce. 

Considering JJ's Second Wind has a similarly long start-up, Soothing Mist may be worth taking if you find yourself in team fights frequently.

feats.name: Tough as Nails
feats.description:
Passive | Raises max Health by 15% but does not heal when first unlocked. 

Subsequent respawns will give you full health (Except in Elimination).
feats.explanation:
More health is always nice. Combined with the Bulk Up and Bastion perks, can make you quite tanky and hard to dislodge from a capture point. It doesn't effect the amount of revenge build up you need to activate revenge, making stalling easier in comparison. 

Don't use it in Elimination, where for some reason, it doesn't work on respawn.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow. 

The feat can almost completely negate damage over time feats like Nail Bomb or Fire Flask, or punishes from bleed-based characters. 

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Fiery Barrage
feats.description:
Cast a 16 meter AOE circle of fireworks, that blinds any opponent entering or leaving the circle, and leaves them OOS. 

Circle lasts for 10 seconds, and can only be used outside.
feats.explanation:
An extremely fast cooldown lets you use this feat with impunity, and it can be used offensively to prevent opponents fleeing (especially useful if you are being ganked and have revenge), or defensively to prevent opponents entering an area without being at a significant disadvantage. 

In Breach, can be used both to attack or defend the Commander by keeping opponents away from him.

feats.name: Fire Flask
feats.description: Throw a projectile that explodes in fire after 1100ms, dealing 20-30 damage within the 10 meter AOE and then 10 fire damage per second over 10 seconds.
feats.explanation:
Despite nerfs, this feat is still a great Tier 4, as it is hard to avoid, can be used inside, and has a big area denial affect. The direct damage is now less likely to kill opponents instantly, but the damage over time and area denial aspects have not been changed, allowing great control of a fight.

Combine with a damage buffing feat (eg. Fury or Inspire) or a defence debuff feat to maximise its potential. If used where opponents cannot get out of the flames, it can still wipe an entire team, but the fire damage can be cleansed by healing feats, allowing it to be countered by some feat combos. 

Also useful in the minion lane to clear or to kill a horde of pikemen, and it is also capable of damaging the ram slightly.

feats.name: Phalanx
feats.description: Grant a 70 health overshield to all alive teammates (yourself included) for 10 seconds.
feats.explanation: A life saving feat that works across the map, and when used right can win a teamfight by itself. An excellent choice, probably best in slot for any character lucky enough to have it.

feats.name: Deadly Duet
feats.description: Passive | Deal 20% more damage in close quarters against an enemy who is alone.
feats.explanation:
The damage boost can be useful if roaming around for solo players to kill or trying to capture a zone from a single defender, but is easily negated if the opponents are in groups and have good coordination. 

More useful in Breach because the larger map makes it more likely to find someone alone. Bounty Hunter is normally a better choice.

feats.name: Bounty Hunter
feats.description: Passive | Gain 16 Health & full Stamina when you kill another Hero.
feats.explanation: Very useful in team fights or anti-ganking where landing a kill can heal you (even under a revenge shield) and allow you to carry on the offensive due to the full stamina regen, or save the need to rotate to a healing point. Even better in Breach, where healing is scarce.

feats.name: Rush
feats.description: For 10 seconds, your sprint speed is boosted by 30%.
feats.explanation: A consistently useful feat. Can help with rotations or to get back into the fight after a respawn, especially on bigger maps, but there is often a better choice, especially on characters that are already fast. Can be useful to capture an offering in Breach or Tribute.

feats.name: Caltrops
feats.description:
Drop caltrops that deal damage 2 damage/second to moving enemies and allies in a 6 meter AOE. 

Caltrops persist for 15 seconds, with the cooldown beginning after they disappear.
feats.explanation:
Extremely useful in a team fight, anti-gank, or even 1v1 scenario (often useful to bait a dodge which can be caught with a GB), and additionally can be used to clear soldiers and pikemen. 

When dropped in the path of enemy pikemen or soldiers, caltrops will completely prevent them from crossing, and can easily kill a whole wave of foes, particularly at chokepoints.

Has now been nerfed with double the cooldown and 10s shorter active duration, but is still a very strong T2 feat and by far Nuxia's best choice in that slot.

feats.name: Executioner's Respite
feats.explanation:
Grants a minimal amount of extra healing from an execution, which is often useless if you are executing on an owned point, or have the Devourer perk active. 

You will only rarely get any value from this feat, so most characters have a stronger T2 available.

feats.name: Thrilling Comeback
feats.description: Passive | Upon unlocking, gives you a cleansing 20 health when you are in Revenge (so you gain the health if you unlock the feat while in revenge).
feats.explanation: A shadow of it's former self, it relies on you getting revenge to get any value, and is typically overshadowed by other feats due to its harsh nerf from 40 to 20 health. Use only if your other options suck.

feats.name: Thread of Fate
feats.description:
Target and bind an enemy for up to 15 seconds. Bound enemy can't jog, sprint, or roll, and can only walk. 

The bind is broken if your opponent moves out of your lock-on range.
feats.explanation:
Prevents an opponent from fleeing, which is extremely useful for ganking, or preventing a low health opponent from disengaging. 

Can be used to great effect with coordinated teammates to guarantee hitting an ally feat, or in a team fight to stop an opponent using unlock rolls to escape ally mix-ups. 

In Breach, it has extra utility in preventing an opponent from capturing the offering, which can swing a match.

feats.name: Slip Through
feats.description: Passive | Your next attack after a dodge deals 30% more damage.
feats.explanation: A decent feat, as it boosts the power of your dodge attacks and deflects, as well as any other damage (eg. from feats) after a dodge.

feats.name: Takedown
feats.description: For 30s, your throws now unbalance enemies (similar to an out of stamina throw).
feats.explanation:
Landing an uninterrupted GB and throw in a team fight is rather unlikely, so this feat rarely sees use at a competitive level - although neither does Nuxia see much play there.

However, if you do get into a 1v1 with this feat active, it can be extremely strong, as in those cases, getting a GB throw is much more possible, and this feat boosts the damage you get from those to all be the equivalent of OOS punishes. In Breach, where 1v1 scenarios are more likely due to the larger maps, it can be consistently useful.

Nuxia's undodgeable heavies become a true nightmare to deal with when takedown is active, and it's likely your opponent will try to parry the move due to the insane damage is provides.

feats.name: Infection
feats.description:
Applies "Corruption" to an enemy, which deals damage over time to the enemy and their allies within a 10 meter AOE, but only if their allies (excluding soldiers) remain within range. 

Deals 8 damage per second for 10 seconds. Has a medium hit reaction when applied to an opponent.
feats.explanation:
A decent damage dealing feat, which can decimate an opposing team in a team fight, or cause them to scatter.  Particularly useful in enclosed spaces where the opponents cannot flee, and can give Nuxia a potent anti-gank, especially combined with Caltrops and/or Thread of Fate. 

Can target an opponent through walls, and the hit reaction can knock an opponent off a ladder, or guarantee an ally attack. 

In Breach, it is fantastic used on the Commander, defenders will not be able to stay close to him without suffering high damage, allowing your team to attack without opposition. However, with players so used to the corruption effect since Warmonger's release, it can be hard to get significant damage from this feat.

feats.name: Regenerate
feats.description:
Passive | Regenerate 15 health every 2 seconds. 

Must be out of guard, and not out of stamina, not sprinting, attacking or any other action, in order to start recovery. 

Takes 3.5 seconds to start regeneration.
feats.explanation:
An underwhelming feat that essentially requires you to not be playing the game in order to get any benefit from it - but does give a big benefit when it is active. 

The only things you can do whilst regenerating, are standing still, or walking. Even sprinting, or climbing a ladder, stops regeneration, so you cannot heal during rotations, unless walking rather than sprinting. 

Can have a niche use to regen health by unlocking at the edge of team fights, and is overall better now that the healing rate of capture zones has been reduced making it worth taking if you lack any better T4s. 

More useful in Breach, where you can walk forward with the ram, (or let it push you), or in Tribute when guarding an offering. But even then, a Tier 4 takes a long time to unlock, so you won't have much time to make use of it.

feats.name: Berzerker
feats.description: For 30 seconds, gain 45% damage reduction and a 20% sprint speed buff.
feats.explanation: A great defensive buff that lasts for a good amount of time, but it doesn't particularly hold a candle to other options like Fear Itself or Fire Flask, considering that the other two feats help your team out, rather than yourself, and the sprint speed component of this feat is still pretty underwhelming. Nuxia might see use out of this feat, but she has no hyperarmor to really utilise the reduction, and a T4 feat isn't the greatest for stalling when she already has caltrops.

feats.name: Qi Trap
feats.description:
Set a trap that highlights an opponent for 45 seconds when triggered, allowing you and all team mates to see them through walls. 

8 meter AOE, does not get used up when triggered, and can trigger for multiple opponents.
feats.explanation: This feat is highly map-dependent, but can be almost brokenly powerful. If placed at the opponents' spawn location it will be able to permanently highlight the entire enemy team on the map, letting your whole team know where they are at any time.

feats.name: Stealth
feats.description:
Passive | Hide yourself from the HUD, Radar & Aim Assist. 

Also hides you from the Oracle's Blessing in Tribute, Marked for Death and Scout
feats.explanation: Can help you to get a surprise attack in, and prevents many debuff feats from targetting you whatsoever. Assists against projectile feats by shortening the range of the snap-on crosshair.

feats.name: Iron Lungs
feats.description: Passive | Able to sprint while out of stamina. Recover stamina faster while running.
feats.explanation:
Basically useless. You can regen stamina whilst sprinting without this feat, and the increased rate is hardly noticable. 

Only conceivable use is to allow you to dodge roll without having to stop sprinting if you go OOS, and allowing you to unlock sprint to avoid OOS pressure from certain characters.

feats.name: Blink
feats.description:
Teleport behind the locked-on hero and perform a Sun Kick, guaranteeing a light follow-up. 

Has the same recovery as a Sun Kick.

Can be dodged up to 566ms after activation.
feats.explanation:
Fantastic synergy with stealth, and excellent cooldown, you can often use this feat to initiate combat with a foe, and have it ready to chase them down if they try to flee. 

Can score ledge kills on opponents facing an edge. The Sun Kick light is guaranteed, and leads into your sweep mixup.

If used out of Qi stance, landing this feat will also trigger your T3 Invigorate, for extra healing, but if used from neutral, it will not. However, deals relatively low damage, can be GB punished on reaction if the opponent sees you using it, and can regularly lose tracking for no apparent reason, leading to frustration.

feats.name: Winner's Advantage
feats.description: Passive | After a successful attack, you deal 20% more damage for 1.5 seconds.
feats.explanation:
In practice, this feat can give your follow-up attacks a decent boost if you can land a second attack in the short window. 

With the CCU improving the ability to land opener attacks, this feat is much more relevant. 

In Breach it gains some utility by letting chain heavies do more damage against pikemen.

feats.name: Thick Skin
feats.description:
Passive | After taking a hit receive 25% less damage for 3 seconds. Triggered by attacks or bashes hitting, being hit by a GB (even if countered), and any feat that causes hitstun. 

Not triggered by chip damage.
feats.explanation:
This feat has recently been changed, and now also triggers after being hit by a bash, or a GB, even if countered, making the damage reduction applicable in many more situations, including bash or GB gank set ups. 

The CCU has also meant that light openers hit a bit more often, buffing chain offence - which this feat works well to help defend against. 

Now that you can more consistently benefit from the damage reduction, this feat is much more worthwhile.

feats.name: Invigorate
feats.description:
Passive | Heal yourself and allies within a 12 meter AOE for 4 health for every attack from Qi stance, even when blocked or parried. 

Cleanses bleed and fire damage.

Also triggered by T2 Blink, if used from Qi stance.
feats.explanation:
This strong feat allows Shaolin to sustain his team during a team fight, and it can also help considerably in a 1v1. It also neuters pressure from damage over time, making it great at countering bleed characters, and fire damage feats.

Getting healed from a blocked or even parried attack means that having a Qi stance heavy parried in a team fight can heal your team more than the net damage of a heavy parry punish. 

Doesn't work on Pikemen or Minions, but does work on Captains.

feats.name: Heal on Block
feats.description: Passive | Blocking regenerates 4 Health.
feats.explanation:
The usefulness of this feat is fairly self-explanatory, and can discourage opponents from attacking you in a 1v1. 

Can also help survivabilty in ganks, as you can heal under the revenge shield. However, in practice, you still will take some chip damage from heavy attacks, and most competent opponents won't be throwing easily blockable lights anyway. 

No longer heals from minion or pikemen attacks, which removes its previous strength in mid.

feats.name: Nukekubi
feats.description:
Passive | Regenerate stamina on successful attacks or bashes. 

Also triggers on any feat that causes hitstun, like projectile feats, and can be used on soldiers. 

Stamina gained seems related to the stagger of the attack, and is normally enough to recoup the entire cost of regular attacks, and some bashes.
feats.explanation: The gained from this feat can be fairly substantial, although it doesn't work on blocked attacks. Still slightly underwhelming for a tier 3, as it rather selfish, but can allow for continuous offence if successful. Works on minions and can allow for efficient mid clearing.

feats.name: Blessed Projection
feats.description: Target an ally anywhere on the map (works through walls), then activate with 1.5 second startup to teleport to their side.
feats.explanation:
Allows extremely rapid rotations, letting you reinforce an ally in trouble, quickly get back to a team fight after respawning, or escape an outnumbered situation. Usefulness varies across maps, being better on the larger ones. 

In Breach, it is more useful due to the larger maps, but also has a niche and extremely powerful use, whereby you can pick up the offering, and immdediately teleport to an ally waiting by the ram or gatehouse, practically guaranteeing the offering for your team, which can have a deciding influence on the match.

feats.name: Slippery
feats.description:
A joke feat that automatically counters guard breaks, if it were possible to manually counter them (guaranteed GBs in vulnerable frames are not stopped). 

Lasts for 30 seconds. Use this if you find pressing counter guardbreak too difficult.
feats.explanation:
Easily the worst feat in the game, and an utter waste of a Tier 4. You should be able to counter all non-guaranteed GBs easily, so this feat provides nothing useful. Why the devs thought to also give it to Shaolin, I have no idea. 

Recently buffed to not be GB vulnerable during activation, this pathetic buff does nothing to elevate this feat from it's current joke-tier uselessness.

feats.name: Scout
feats.description:
All enemies across the map are effected by "Marked for Death", and show up on the Radar and are visible through walls.

Enemy attacks cost 25% more stamina, and they take 15% increased damage for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation: A sub par Tier 4 feat that can help in critical team fights, but is let down by its small effect and short duration. It is good to use when the opponents are breaking - both to kill them more quickly, and to see if one of them is going to capture a point, and head them off in advance. Short duration requires intelligent use.

feats.name: Fiery Tusk
feats.description: Throw a projectile that deals 10 damage, and can explode for an additional +15 damage if the target is burning.
feats.explanation:
Short cooldown allows this feat to be used frequently, and it can be useful for interrupting an opponent due to the quick start-up. 

Can do a decent chunk of damage on a burning opponent, so combos well with your T2. 

However the damage usually is very low, and it may be better to take Bounty Hunter, especially in Breach.

feats.name: Fast Recovery
feats.description: Passive | Stamina regenerates twice as fast. Also works when exhausted.
feats.explanation: Allows you to be a bit more aggressive with stamina-intensive attacks, and escape OOS state much faster. Also useful for zoning more frequently in mid lane or team fights. If you take this feat, there is no need to bother with the Fresh Focus perk.

feats.name: Qilin Ruse
feats.description: Throw a trap that explodes after 900ms and burns targets within a 6 meter AOE, dealing 30 fire damage, that ticks down over 4 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A very useful feat, which can either be used as a medium damage projectie or as a trap. This trap is comparatively easy to spot, but is very hard to avoid taking damage from it even if the opponent sees it, as it will apply fire damage even if they roll. 

Can be useful placed in minions to slow down an opponent from retaking mid. Short cooldown allows frequent use.

It does a great chunk of damage, which is easily confirmed by an ally, making it useful for ganks, and with standardisation of speed to 700ms, can be used more easily in some 1v1 scenarios.

feats.name: Scorching Deluge
feats.description:
Causes fire to fall on every enemy within a 16 meter AOE centered on the Zhanhu, taking 1200ms for the fire to land. 

Fire strikes each do 20 direct damage and an additional 40 fire damage, lasting 8 seconds, and leave the ground on fire in a 4 meter AOE for 10 seconds. 

Only works if the user and opponent(s) are outside, and can only be activated if there is an opponent within range.
feats.explanation: Slow start-up, and small AOEs make this feat fairly easy to avoid, and it does low damage compared to other direct damage T4s. Can be useful in a team fight, but only if that fight happens outside.

feats.name: Last Laugh
feats.description: Passive | Drop an explosive on death. Cannot activate if executed. Deals 20-100 damage depending on how far the enemy is from the center of the 10 meter AOE.
feats.explanation:
Because this feat requires your death, and can be prevented from working by an execution, it is somewhat underwhelming. 

Ensuring that you don't die prematurely or where the grenade is ineffective (eg. fall damage) can be challenging. But running into a gank, intentionally dying to a light attack, and getting a quad kill is possibly one of the most satisfying moments this game can offer. 

Because the commander's overhead unblockable will not execute, you can easily do great damage to him, and kill any defenders that are clustered nearby.

Can be used in chain instead of Pistol Blast with the same link speeds and chaining options. Confirmed on landed heavies.
feats.explanation: Great for long range peel, initiating fights, adding damage to punishes instead of a regular gunshot, and for interrupting opponents in hyperarmor. Relatively quick cooldown allows for regular use, and being able to use this feat in chain and dodge cancel the recoveries gives it a lot of flexibility.

feats.name: Tireless

feats.explanation:
Allows you to attack a bit more frequently, but not all that impressive.

feats.explanation: Very slow activation, and small radius makes this AOE trivial to avoid. Combine with comparatively low damage, and this is a very sub-par feat.

feats.name: Bloodlust
feats.description: Passive | Killing heroes grants a 20% attack boost, and 20% damage reduction, for 10 seconds.
feats.explanation: This is a signficant temporary attack and defence boost, which can really help in both anti-gank and team-fight scenarios.

Fire a bullet with light hitstun dealing 10 direct and 30 bleed damage over 10 seconds. The bullet can bounce up to 3 times to hit opponents within 5 meters, ignoring Stealth.

Can be used in chain instead of Pistol Blast with the same link speeds and chaining options. Confirmed on landed heavies.
feats.explanation: High damage to a potentially large number of opponents, with a fast activtion speed and flexible use due to activation in chain, and dodge recovery cancel or chaining after use. feats.description:
Fires a bomb, that explodes 1133ms after landing, dealing 40 damage, and knocking down every opponent in the ~12 meter AOE.

feats.explanation: Very large AOE makes avoiding damage from this feat extremely difficult, and the knockdown can confirm a lot of damage used correctly. The 90 second cooldown is reset when you reach 70 HP, though the UI does not show this if the 90s CD is already triggered.
feats.explanation:
Gives significantly improved ability to survive in a team fight or makes you into a stall monster if the opponents think about ganking you, especially if you're able to proc the reset condition of 70 health with healing from feats like Vital Leech or Thrilling Comeback.

Be careful not to be hit by an attack that kills you before reaching critical health, as the feat will not trigger that way. Neither will it trigger from bleed, chip damage, or sacrifice, so plan accordingly.

feats.name: Sunshine Strength
feats.description: Passive |  After a kill, gain a buff that lasts until death, dependent on the mode you were in when you got the kill. A kill in Staff Mode grants a 10% defence buff, and a kill in Axe Mode grants a 10% damage buff. Both of these buffs can be acquired in a single life.
feats.explanation: An incredibly powerful T1 feat, that allows for a permanent buff as long as you can kill two enemies in both Staff and Axe Modes, leading to much better trades and health swings in Medjay's favour when teamfighting - which already were great.

feats.name: Body Count
feats.description: Passive | Killing a soldier or pikeman through any means (including feats) grants you 1 health and 1 stamina.
feats.explanation:
A decent pick for mid lane characters in Dominion, this feat allows for some sustain whilst clearing minions, but is no longer really enough to stay in mid indefinitely. 

In Breach, this feat is extremely underwhelming, as you have to kill 10 pikemen to heal a single poke's worth of damage. 

May allow you to clear a bit more before having to head to the heal zone, but many other Tier 1s are superior in this mode.

feats.name: Iron Lungs
feats.description: Passive | Able to sprint while out of stamina. Recover stamina faster while running.
feats.explanation:
Basically useless. You can regen stamina whilst sprinting without this feat, and the increased rate is hardly noticable. 

Only conceivable use is to allow you to dodge roll without having to stop sprinting if you go OOS, and allowing you to unlock sprint to avoid OOS pressure from certain characters.

feats.name: Moonlight Drain
feats.description: Passive | Upon landing a bash applies a debuff to the opponent, depending on the mode you are in. Landing a bash in Staff Mode lowers opponent defence by 15% for 5 seconds, and landing a bash in Axe Mode lowers their attack by 15% for 5 seconds.
feats.explanation:
A feat that bolsters the ability of Medjay's gank in Staff Mode, increasing your ally's damage for no extra revenge - this makes his ganks even more lethal.

Axe Mode's version is a bit more underwhelming, but is still nice to reduce the damage you take from a dodge attack in your infinite bash mixup.

feats.name: Executioner's Respite
feats.explanation:
Grants a minimal amount of extra healing from an execution, which is often useless if you are executing on an owned point, or have the Devourer perk active. 

You will only rarely get any value from this feat, so most characters have a stronger T2 available.

feats.name: Thrilling Comeback
feats.description: Passive | Upon unlocking, gives you a cleansing 20 health when you are in Revenge (so you gain the health if you unlock the feat while in revenge).
feats.explanation: A shadow of it's former self, it relies on you getting revenge to get any value, and is typically overshadowed by other feats due to its harsh nerf from 40 to 20 health. Use only if your other options suck.

feats.name: Scarab Relief
feats.description:
In Staff Mode: After 700ms, heal yourself and all allies within an X meter AOE for 15 health. Also cleanses bleed or fire damage.

In Axe Mode: After 100ms, recover 25 health, and cleanse bleed or fire damage from yourself.
feats.explanation:
A very nice feat, combining Draconite Mist with Second Wind, allowing for you to decide if you want to heal your team and cleanse them of their wounds, or use it as a personal heal if needed.

The inability to pick a personal heal/group heal without swapping stance does however leave you quite vulnerable, and is pretty predictable, so be cautious.

feats.name: Heal on Block
feats.description: Passive | Blocking regenerates 4 Health.
feats.explanation:
The usefulness of this feat is fairly self-explanatory, and can discourage opponents from attacking you in a 1v1. 

Can also help survivabilty in ganks, as you can heal under the revenge shield. However, in practice, you still will take some chip damage from heavy attacks, and most competent opponents won't be throwing easily blockable lights anyway. 

No longer heals from minion or pikemen attacks, which removes its previous strength in mid.

feats.name: Second Wind
feats.description: Recover 30 health instantly on use, and removes any bleed or fire damage.
feats.explanation:
Despite being nerfed, Second Wind still heals you a decent amount, and the cooldown still allows frequent use, meaning that it is still consistently useful. 

It is fast enough to be usable with only a small break in combat, and if you're clever, can even be used to bait an attack to punish if the opponent is slow. 

The feat can almost completely negate damage over time feats like Nail Bomb or Fire Flask, or punishes from bleed-based characters. 

In Breach it becomes even more useful due to the scarcity of healing.

feats.name: Astral Manifestation
feats.description:
In Staff Mode: Throw a Grenade that explodes dealing 55 damage to all opponents in a X meter AOE.

In Axe Mode: Throw a pair of axes that deal 55 damage.
feats.explanation:
Post nerfs - the axe mode is now very underwhelming, performing like a pre-nerf longbow, which was a strong feat, but not an OP feat in the T3 slot - this is now a T4 providing that sort of value.

The Staff version of the T4 has been buffed marginally to compensate, but still underperforms when compared to something like LB's t4, which has 4 charges and /more/ damage.

feats.description:
Call a catapult on the targeted 8 meter AOE, dealing 40-200 damage to everyone standing within it based on their distance to the center. 

Can only be used outside, and the projectile takes 2000ms to land and do damage.
feats.explanation:
A very underwhelming Tier 4 feat, as the time between the circle appearing and the catapult landing is enough to allow any opponent to escape the danger zone (unless they are unbalanced or blocked in by allies). 

Slightly more utility in Breach, as it can damage the ram, but does rather unimpressive damage to the commander, on the rare occasions he doesn't run out of the AOE.

feats.name: Arrow Storm
feats.description:
5 waves of 50 damage arrow showers over a 15 meter AOE. 

First wave takes 1100ms to land, with each subsequent wave taking another 1300ms. 

Can only be used outside.
feats.explanation:
It can be hard to hit aware opponents with this feat, as it can be fairly easily avoided, unless they are engaged by allies. 

The large AOE makes it great for clearing mid, and it can kill a lot of pikemen, and do very good damage to the ram. One wave of arrows is rarely enough to kill an opponent, and the feat also does considerable friendly fire damage. 

However, with careful targeting it is still capable of wiping an entire team if they are badly positioned.

feats.name: Gravity's Pull
feats.description:
500ms bash that throws your opponent behind you and deals 15 damage.

Can be dodged 400ms before the hit.
feats.explanation:
This T1 feat is still an excellent choice, as it does good damage on a decent cooldown, and is an excellent ganking tool due to resetting hitstun and confirming an ally attack. 

As it is a 500ms bash from neutral, most players will be unable to react to it, and whilst it is vulnerable to interruption, if it is interrupted before impact, it will not go on cooldown. It can also be used whilst the Afeera is OOS, although her stamina will not recover whilst she is in the animation. The damage is dealt at the end of the animation, so using it in a teamfight or careless allies means it is likely to be interrupted - and if the pin animation is interrupted, it will go on cooldown.

feats.name: Fortune's Favor
feats.description: Passive | After landing an attack (bashes included), gain a 20% defense buff for 5 seconds.

Bash that initiates Fleet Foot with Full Block Stance that has superior block properties (this has 400ms startup), forces fleet foot to be active for 400ms if the feat triggers it.

Fleet Foot portion can be soft-feinted into Astro Flip or hard feinted, which will not consume the feat.

Once the Afeera is close to the target, a 500ms bash is sent out, which deals 20 damage, throws the opponent in front of you and confirms the next attack (but the left heavy does not wallsplat). 

Bash can be dodged 400ms before the hit.
feats.explanation:
Much like the tier 1 feat, this does good damage and can confirm ally damage making it a very strong gank tool. Additionally it can be used when OOS, but that will forgoe the confirmed finisher after the bash lands.

The full block property is great, but nowhere near as safe as it once was at 0ms startup, or as potent of an option select.

feats.description:
Passive | Raises max Health by 15% but does not heal when first unlocked. 

Subsequent respawns will give you full health (Except in Elimination).

More health is always nice. Combined with the Bulk Up and Bastion perks, can make you quite tanky and hard to dislodge from a capture point. It doesn't effect the amount of revenge build up you need to activate revenge, making stalling easier in comparison.

Throws a shield at a target, which inflicts 30 damage and 40% defense debuff that lasts for 20s. The shield can bounce to nearby allies of the hit target. 

Be aware that this feat can hit your allies, and then bounce onto other allies or yourself, applying the debuff to your own team, so use with caution.

Whilst it does direct damage, and now has a comparable 40% debuff for 20s, it is still harder to land than a simple AOE, and because it is applied on the opponent directly, they can die early so you don't get the full duration of usage.

This makes it one of the few T4 feats that can actively be a detriment to your whole team. Be very careful using this feat, as it can backfire very easily.

feats.explanation:

After the normal respawn timer, and if you are >Xm from opponents or allies, activate the feat to revive at your current location. After 60s, or if your team enters breaking, you will be respawned as normal.

One of the most divisive feats in the game - this thing is Ocelotl's only real feat choice (otherwise you'll be using Tireless) and yet it can bring both an incredible benefit with proper use, changing the way the enemy team plays by delaying their rotations due to the fear of you backcap respawning, especially on maps like Sanctuary Bridge - though at the same time, this feat can easily lead to you feeding more and more kills to the enemy team as you don't spawn with full HP unless you take way too much time.

Set a trap with a 4 meter AOE, that deals 25 damage, pins the target in place for 2 seconds and leaves them unable to block, parry or dodge. Can only have one Bear Trap active at a time.

1400ms activation time for Berserker/Shaman, 2700ms activation time for Raider.
feats.explanation:
A great feat for defending a zone, or protecting yourself as you clear mid, as in addittion to the damage, it can guarantee a heavy attack or ledging bash. 

Maintains the Out of Lock state, which can guarantee a large punish if the opponent was unlocked before they were caught. 

Can even be used in combat with a little finesse. Like all traps, the damage log can be used to tell you that it has been triggered at a distance. 

The main disadvantages are the long cooldown, and that it is fairly easy to avoid if spotted, so make sure to hide it in scenery as best you can.

feats.description: Passive | Killing an opponent grants a 25% damage boost and a 25% speed buff, which lasts for 20 seconds.
feats.explanation: This is bloodlust but with the caveat of buffing your speed, rather than defense, and being a T3 feat. feats.explanation:

It is even stronger when used with a hazard or ledge to confirm an instant kill. Trapper's Reach is very comparable to Medjay's Axe Stance's Astral Manifestation, although it needs more careful usage to maximise its potential.

feats.name: Misthia Ward
feats.description:
Passive | Gain a 50% damage reduction buff for 5 seconds after superior blocking an attack.

Superior blocking another attack whilst this feat is active will re-activate the feat, granting another 5 second buff.
feats.explanation:
A very strong T2 feat, particularly when in out-numbered scenarios. The potent damage reduction requires the ganking opponents to pause and gives you a 10 second window to breathe every time you full block. It is almost as strong in team fights, as it allows you to counterattack from a full block without worrying too much about being peeled, or eating a large hitbox attack.
